===== docs\api\README.md =====

# API boundaries and capacity replay contract

NestJS is authoritative. Next rewrites `/api/*` to its configured internal origin. `PUBLIC_APP_URL` must match the browser Origin exactly. Better Auth cookies are HttpOnly; account status, session expiry and privileged MFA are checked server-side. Unsafe methods require approved Origin and JSON; application mutations additionally require `X-CSRF-Token` from `GET /api/v1/me`. Never log that response/token. Same-origin cookies remain browser-managed.

Routes are defined in `apps/api/src/modules/{auth,users,organizations,artisans,governance,commerce}/*.controller.ts` and the auth gateway allowlist. Shared strict schemas in `packages/contracts/src` are the executable request contracts; response projection types avoid exposing credentials. There is no upload or wearable endpoint; the isolated synthetic commerce routes are listed below. No generated OpenAPI is configured; do not describe these TypeScript contracts as OpenAPI.

| Area | Representative routes | Scope |
|---|---|---|
| Health | GET `/api/health/live`, `/api/health/ready` | Public; ready checks PostgreSQL |
| Session | GET/PATCH `/api/v1/me`, GET/DELETE `/api/v1/me/sessions[/:id]` | Own verified account |
| Organizations | `/api/v1/organizations`, `/:id`, `/:id/members`, `/:id/invitations` | Membership and operation permission |
| Administration | `/api/v1/admin/organizations`, approvals, users, audit | Platform policies and MFA; no implicit artisan access |
| Artisan | `/api/v1/artisans/me`, `/skills`, `/capacity`, `/associations`, `/delegations` | Owner |
| Assistance | `/api/v1/artisans/:id`, `/:id/skills`, `/:id/capacity` | Owner or current explicit consent/delegation scope |
| Governance | Privacy requests, support cases, consents and audit controllers | Own subject or explicitly scoped staff policies |

Consult controller decorators for exact methods and nested route suffixes. Each identifier passes `resourceIdSchema`; request/list schemas cap input sizes and reject unknown fields. Body limit is 32 KiB. Rate limits are enforced in Nest on direct and rewritten requests.

`POST /api/v1/artisans/me/capacity` and `POST /api/v1/artisans/:id/capacity` accept an optional `Idempotency-Key` of 16..128 ASCII letters/digits/underscore/hyphen. Existing clients without keys retain revision behavior. The browser uses UUID keys and retains one for the same payload during a failed request while the form stays mounted. Navigating/reloading loses that pending browser key; persist/reuse it in an API caller if recovery must survive reload.

A successful first call and authorized identical replay both return 201 and the same original JSON capacity projection (including original `supersededAt`). A changed parsed payload with the same scoped key returns 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`; malformed key returns 400. Key reuse by a different actor/profile has a distinct scope and grants no access. Replay still rejects revoked consent, missing skill, invalid session or delegation. Outcomes are not automatically expired. The key is not stored or logged in plaintext.

Capacity input: `craftSkillId`, `unitType` HOURS/PIECES, numeric `quantity` at most two decimal places 0..100000, ISO `effectiveFrom` and `effectiveTo`. Quantity responses are decimal strings. No quantity is inferred from wearable data.

Errors contain `code`, safe `message`, optional field issues and `requestId`; the response header `X-Request-ID` matches. 401 means invalid session, 403 denied permission/origin/CSRF, 400 invalid input, 409 conflicting state/key, 429 rate limited (`Retry-After`), 503 dependency unavailable. Errors never return exception text or upstream credentials.

## Synthetic commerce contracts

All routes below are relative to `/api/v1/commerce`, require the independent Nest session/CSRF/origin boundary, and reject unknown input fields. Every POST/PATCH requires `Idempotency-Key`; missing/invalid keys return 400. Successful POSTs return 201; draft PATCH returns 200. The command result is `{id,version}`; reload `GET /workspace` for the current safe projection. Resource role checks happen before replay, and stale `version` returns 409. Lists are bounded to 100 records each; no arbitrary client tenant filter is accepted.

| Method / route | Contract | Authorized operation |
|---|---|---|
| GET `/workspace` | `CommerceWorkspaceView` | Current buyer/internal memberships and own artisan profile; safe role-scoped lists |
| POST `/rfqs` | `rfqCreateSchema` | Approved BUYER creates synthetic draft, selecting an approved internal operator and active craft |
| PATCH `/rfqs/:id` | `rfqEditSchema` | Buyer edits DRAFT only; immutable owner/operator/provenance |
| POST `/rfqs/:id/actions` | `rfqActionSchema` | Buyer submit/accept/decline; production review; finance quote/expire |
| POST `/offers` | `offerCreateSchema` | Assigned production manager reserves selected declared capacity and issues immutable terms |
| POST `/offers/:id/actions` | `offerActionSchema` | Owner artisan accept/decline; production expire after deadline |
| POST `/batches/:id/actions` | `batchActionSchema` | Owner production/submission/rework decisions, assigned production/QA actions by role |
| POST `/batches/:id/progress` | `progressSchema` | Owner reports cumulative `produced`, never a delta |
| POST `/batches/:id/inspections` | `inspectionSchema` | Assigned QA records reconciled approved/rejected/pending snapshot and defect reason |
| POST `/orders/:id/actions` | `orderActionSchema` | Current role for funding, release, QA, logistics, buyer receipt, finance reconciliation/closure |
| POST `/payments` | `paymentCreateSchema` | Assigned finance schedules `BUYER_RECEIPT` or `ARTISAN_PAYOUT`; payout batch must belong to order |
| POST `/payments/:id/actions` | `paymentActionSchema` | Assigned finance progresses an isolated synthetic payment; settled requires `SIMULATED_SETTLEMENT` |

All exact fields/types are in `packages/contracts/src/commerce/contracts.ts`; state/role edges and money/quantity semantics are documented in [commerce architecture](../architecture/commerce.md). Dates are ISO timestamps, amounts are TND strings, quantities are whole pieces, all commercial `provenance` inputs must be `SYNTHETIC`. A positive quote has a future expiry before delivery. Offer terms include quantity, unit/total pay, effort range, expiry/deadline, specification, materials, rework and payment conditions before voluntary acceptance.

Buyer projections contain their own RFQs/orders/receipts and omit artisan offers/batches/payouts. Artisans receive their own terms, production and payouts without buyer quote/receipts or other artisans. QA cannot read individual money columns/payment records; production/finance see offer pay as required to create/reconcile terms. Draft RFQs remain private until submission. Platform ADMIN or organization-manager status alone grants no operational role. Individual wearable fields have no contract or persistence column and are rejected by strict schemas.


## Reports, CSV and transactional inbox

- `GET /api/v1/commerce/orders/:id/report`: current approved buyer membership or assigned internal operational role required; 403 for a foreign order or artisan whole-order access. Pending projections return `metrics: null`, status PENDING. Existing projections return `asOf`, definitionVersion 1, SYNTHETIC/SIMULATED metrics and CURRENT/STALE based on outstanding events for the owning buyer organization. Buyer finance includes only its own receipts; FINANCE_MANAGER sees aggregate artisan liabilities/payouts; QA/logistics/production without finance receive no money aggregate. Unknown costs/hours/verified settlement are null, never invented zeros.
- `GET /api/v1/commerce/orders/:id/report.csv`: identical server authorization/minimization; attachment filename synthetic-commerce.csv, text/csv and no-store. Fixed registry fields and integer cells only. A pending report exports the header without invented metrics; load the JSON/UI status first. No file upload or arbitrary filesystem path is supported.
- `GET /api/v1/commerce/inbox`: up to 100 newest static event-code/time notices, scoped using current approved memberships. Buyer notices exclude private offer/batch/payout events; artisan notices cover only its own work. Finance/production operator notices require assigned internal roles. Revocation removes organization notices from subsequent reads. A user cannot request another account's inbox or pass a tenant override.

All are protected Nest reads and require valid active sessions. There is no public analytics rebuild/replay endpoint. Reports and notices appear only after the separate worker processes committed events. Queue status/backfill are trusted CLI commands described in operations. These features never ingest monitoring fields.
## Buyer craft examples (#31)

`GET /api/v1/commerce/catalog` requires a current active verified session and returns at most 100 active craft categories, descriptions and version-1 synthetic example fixtures. Examples contain unit, specification/design suggestions, local illustrative image/alternative text (or null), indicative lead-time range/assumptions and `ILLUSTRATIVE`/`UNAVAILABLE` status. This shared projection contains no organization records, artisan identity/capacity, stock, price or confirmed supply.

`POST /api/v1/commerce/rfqs` additionally accepts optional `catalogExampleId`. The API checks the current active craft and requires a known illustrative example of that craft before invoking the existing transactional replay-safe command. The buyer must provide valid specification/design requirements, quantity, destination and future delivery deadline. Example selection is an initial suggestion, not a reservation, quote or approved SKU. The selection ID participates in the command fingerprint; only the buyer-confirmed RFQ fields are persisted. Draft edits retain their existing strict schema. Manual RFQs remain available without an example; live SKU/version lineage belongs to E20 and is not implemented by this route.


===== docs\architecture\commerce.md =====

# Synthetic commerce: domain rules and implemented boundaries

This bounded implementation completes the domain and critical-journey scope of #32/#88. All commercial rows have immutable `SYNTHETIC` provenance, enforced by PostgreSQL CHECK constraints. Settlement evidence is always `SIMULATED_SETTLEMENT`. There is no banking adapter, real contract execution, monitoring upload, verified-hardware claim or assertion that simulated receipts are real money.

The states below come from sections 3–5 of the product's `HirfaCare_FINAL_Detailed_Backlog.md`, inspected in the optional sibling docs checkout. The original requirements for #32/#88/#195 are preserved in `../engineering/issues/`. The implemented transitions live in `packages/contracts/src/commerce/domain.ts`, independently of Prisma/Nest/React. Strict wire contracts and safe projection types live in `commerce/contracts.ts`. Nest's `CommerceService` invokes these rules within the existing serialized IAM transaction; state, command outcome, audit and metadata-only outbox commit atomically.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
 Buyer[Buyer RFQ / exact quote decision] --> API[Nest session + CSRF + resource roles]
 Artisan[Artisan voluntary offer / cumulative progress] --> API
 Operator[Operator funding / production / QA / logistics] --> API
 API --> Commands[CommerceService commands]
 Commands --> Pure[Pure domain transitions and reconciliation]
 Commands --> DB[(PostgreSQL synthetic records)]
 DB --> Audit[Transactional audit + outbox]
 Worker[Local receipt worker] --> Audit
```

| Entity | Supported normal path | Role / guarded branches |
|---|---|---|
| RFQ | DRAFT → SUBMITTED → UNDER_REVIEW → QUOTED → ACCEPTED | Buyer drafts/submits/accepts/declines; production reviews; finance quotes/expires. Drafts are private. Accepted quote creates one order. Quote must be current and unexpired. |
| Offer | PLANNED → OFFERED → ACCEPTED | Production creates immutable offered terms/reservation; only the owner artisan accepts/declines. Expiry releases tentative capacity. Decline causes no eligibility penalty. |
| Order | APPROVED → FUNDING_CONFIRMED → PLANNING → IN_PRODUCTION → QUALITY_REVIEW → READY_TO_SHIP → IN_TRANSIT → DELIVERED → BUYER_ACCEPTED → SETTLED → CLOSED | Funding/settlement/closure require finance; planning/release production; shipment approval QA; shipment/delivery logistics; receipt acceptance buyer. |
| Batch | ACCEPTED → MATERIAL_READY → IN_PROGRESS → SUBMITTED → INSPECTION → APPROVED → COMPLETED | Material readiness/completion production; progress/submission artisan; inspection/QA inspector. INSPECTION → REWORK_REQUESTED → IN_PROGRESS requires explicit owner rework acceptance. Rework may be disputed. |
| Synthetic payment | SCHEDULED → APPROVED → INITIATED → SETTLED | Finance only; scheduled/approved can be cancelled, initiated can fail/be disputed. Settled is terminal and requires explicitly simulated evidence. Buyer receipt and artisan payout are separate kinds. |

Every unlisted edge, same-state duplicate with a new command key, forbidden role or terminal-state mutation is rejected. The source's `AMENDED` order state is recognized but has no enabled edge: contract amendment/reapproval needs its own reviewed workflow and cannot be reached through a status toggle. Controlled cancellation is restricted to an unstarted APPROVED order without accepted/reserved work, receipts, artisan obligations or pending payments. Disputed order/batch/payment branches preserve history and block settlement/closure; no automatic dispute resolution or write-off exists.

## Exact money and quantities

TND uses bigint millimes throughout commands and PostgreSQL BIGINT; 1 TND = 1000 millimes. Decimal API/UI strings have at most three digits on input and exactly three on output. Existing `parseTnd`, `formatTnd`, `addTnd`, `prorateTnd` reject precision loss, negatives and overflow beyond 9223372036854775807 millimes. Proration uses HALF_UP once at the millime boundary. Offer pay and payouts use integer `unitPayMillimes × wholeUnits`; no floating-point totals occur. Buyer quote totals never leak through artisan projections.

Whole piece quantities are safe integers 0..1,000,000; requested/offer quantities must be positive. Capacity remains an independently consented decimal declaration, never sensor-derived. A piece declaration covering the delivery date is selected explicitly; reservations and accepted commitments across all orders referencing that declaration cannot exceed its quantity. Future declared windows can be planned. This conservative prototype reserves against a selected period without multiplying weekly capacity by period length; calendar optimization/capacity amendments are separate work.

For an order:

```text
reserved + allocated <= requested
produced <= allocated
submitted <= produced
approved + rejected + pending = submitted
delivered <= approved
```

`reserved` includes unexpired PLANNED/OFFERED quantities; `allocated` includes explicitly ACCEPTED offers. Decline/expiry frees only tentative reservations. Production reports are **cumulative**: previous <= new <= accepted quantity. Each submission establishes pending QA counts; produced and QA-approved remain distinct. Inspection attempts are immutable, versioned snapshots. Approved quantities never decrease; reinspection replaces the current reconciliation while preserving previous attempts, preventing repeated counting. Each batch has exactly one accepted offer.

Artisan eligible obligation is derived independently of buyer receipt timing: QA-approved units × immutable accepted unit pay under the displayed synthetic milestone policy. Multiple partial payment records are allowed, but settled + outstanding scheduled/approved/initiated/disputed reservations + a new amount cannot exceed eligible value. Failed/cancelled payment records preserve history without reserving more funds. Buyer receipts reconcile against the accepted quote; payouts reconcile against the selected batch, whose parent order is checked server-side.

Shipment requires the full requested quantity to be QA-approved with no rejected/pending units. Settlement requires full delivered/buyer-accepted quantity, exact buyer receipts, every artisan obligation covered and no disputes or pending payments. Closure additionally records an explicit synthetic material/returns disposition note. That note is an operator attestation, not a physical inventory measurement. Partial-fulfillment contract remedies, amended pricing, real accounting/tax and evidence-backed bank settlement are outside this prototype; conservative guards reject paths that would hide obligations.

## Authorization, replay and persistence

Roles come from current approved organization memberships. Buyer access requires BUYER in the owning buyer organization. Operator permissions require the actual PRODUCTION_MANAGER / QUALITY_INSPECTOR / FINANCE_MANAGER / INVENTORY_LOGISTICS_COORDINATOR role in the assigned INTERNAL organization. Manager/global ADMIN alone grants none of these operations. Artisan decisions/progress require the profile owner; association coordinators cannot accept on their behalf. Acceptance also requires current profile-processing consent. New offers require active skill, consent, usable capacity and active verified artisan account.

All commerce mutations require a bounded `Idempotency-Key`. Scope binds actor, resolved resource, operation and canonical validated payload. Replay rechecks current ownership/membership/role before returning the original `{id,version}` result. Required input `version` rejects stale writes; identical committed requests with the same key replay even though the record has advanced. Keys, outcomes and snapshots remain private; no automatic ledger expiry is configured. Browser retries keep the key while the same mounted form retries identical input; page reload loses that transient browser key.

Additive migration `202610200002_synthetic_commerce` creates six related tables with foreign keys, unique order-per-RFQ/batch-per-offer/inspection-version constraints, state/provenance/money/count checks. No existing record is rewritten. API errors use safe 400 validation, 403 denied role/consent, 404 missing record and 409 transition/version/reconciliation conflicts. Events contain metadata only; free-text specifications, terms, QA reasons, amounts and wearable values are not copied to the outbox.


===== docs\architecture\README.md =====

# Implemented architecture

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Browser --> Next[Next.js pages and same-origin API rewrite]
  Next --> Nest[NestJS API: session, CSRF, RBAC, strict Zod]
  Nest --> Commands[Organization, artisan and governance services]
  Commands --> Rules[Pure shared domain rules]
  Commands --> TX[Prisma IAM transaction and advisory locks]
  TX --> DB[(PostgreSQL)]
  TX --> Audit[Append-only audit and metadata-only outbox]
  Worker[Separate local database worker] --> Audit
  Worker --> Receipt[Atomic notices, projections and unique receipts]
  Simulator[Independent fixed local wearable simulator] --> Local[Private bounded in-memory weekly summary]
  Nest --> Auth[Better Auth and SMTP]
```

One website repository contains three application/shared packages; contracts include pure `domain.ts`. No new broker or service infrastructure is required. Browser code never reads PostgreSQL. No AI/IoT runtime integration exists. Organization membership/approval and artisan ownership or consent-bound delegation define scopes; global administrators do not inherit artisan/organization access.

The domain module preserves actual organization rules: draft/rejected profiles may be edited/submitted; pending/suspended organizations may be approved/rejected; only approved organizations may be suspended. Suspended-to-rejected is existing behavior. The synthetic RFQ/order/offer/batch/QA/payment implementation and its pure guarded machines are described in [commerce architecture](commerce.md).

Capacity remains voluntary and independent of sensors. Periods are half-open; adjacent periods do not overlap. A revision must exactly match an overlapping current period, and supersedes its metadata without deleting history. Quantities use exact decimal strings for PostgreSQL Decimal(12,2), 0..100000 with at most two fractional digits.

TND helpers accept canonical nonnegative decimal strings with at most three fractional digits. Internal values are bigint millimes (1000 per TND), capped at signed 64-bit maximum 9223372036854775807 millimes. API/UI serialization is a three-decimal string, never bigint JSON or binary float. Inputs with excess precision, signs, whitespace, exponent or leading zeros are rejected. Rational proration rounds HALF_UP once at the final millime; addition checks overflow. These utilities are used by synthetic quote, offer and settlement commands. They do not implement live money movement.

Capacity keys bind actor, resolved profile, operation and SHA-256 key hash; canonical parsed-payload hashes detect conflicts. Outcomes, mutation, audit and event commit together. IAM locks serialize current callers and a unique index backs the ledger. Resource access, active session, consent and active skill are rechecked even for replay. Outcomes retain the original response indefinitely by default; do not purge until a reviewed deduplication/retention window exists. Never use this helper outside the documented transaction and lock order.

All existing calls to the IAM `audit()` helper now insert version-1 outbox records in the same transaction. Historical audits and other legacy logging paths are not backfilled. Events allow only IDs, action/type, tenant scope, timestamps and correlation metadata. No free text, snapshots, capacity values, monitoring or health fields are copied. Actor/profile IDs remain personal identifiers, so the queue and receipts stay private and require retention review. The consumer never aggregates event payloads: it resolves commerce IDs to authoritative SYNTHETIC records, validates tenant/provenance and builds a versioned SIMULATED projection. Non-commerce events only receive internal receipts. Monitoring data has no input path.

The worker delivers commerce event codes to scoped in-app notices, rebuilds per-order metrics and writes a unique receipt in one transaction. PENDING/RETRY rows are claimed with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`; the database lock is the running state. A killed transaction releases its claim. A savepoint rolls back failed local consumer effects; delivery status, attempts, duration and a fixed error code are recorded. Five failed attempts enter FAILED, with exponential delays (2^attempt seconds, capped at one hour). CLI replay resets the attempt budget for a selected failed event. Receipts deduplicate at-least-once delivery. External notification delivery and distributed leases are not implemented; the row lock provides crash recovery for local transactions. The same existing outbox provides bounded retryable ETL without another queue. Shared IAM locks deliberately serialize current prototype commands/consumers; throughput must be measured before any scaling claim. Existing invitation/support email remains outside this worker and is not claimed replay-safe.


## Rebuildable reports and local simulation

`CommerceProjection` is a disposable per-order read model; `CommerceNotice` stores only fixed event codes and audience scopes. `jobs/commerce-consumer.ts` rebuilds metrics from orders/batches/offers/payments plus immutable shipment/acceptance audit milestones. Source ledger tables are never updated by ETL. The version-1 shared registry in contracts defines exact millime strings and distinct produced/submitted/approved/shipped/received/accepted numerators with requested quantity denominators. Reporting window is order lifetime through `asOf`, timezone UTC. Unknown actual costs/hours/verified settlement remain null with UNAVAILABLE coverage. No real payment is represented as verified.

Current approved organization memberships are rechecked transactionally on reports/CSV/inbox. Buyer reports omit artisan earnings/payments; finance can see the scoped synthetic aggregate; QA/logistics receive fulfillment only; artisans cannot query a whole-order report. Notices expose fixed labels/times, not arbitrary audit snapshots or target IDs. CSV cells are fixed metric names, enum units and integers; no user-entered spreadsheet formulas. `worker --rebuild-analytics` supports bounded safe backfill without duplicate notices. See [operations](../operations/README.md).

The independent IoT repository’s `simulator` project has no commerce/database/network dependency and is invoked only explicitly through its local CLI/tests. It cannot feed analytics or mutate voluntary capacity. Device adapters, configuration assumptions and simulator/physical evidence boundaries are documented in [firmware](../firmware/README.md).


===== docs\deployment\README.md =====

# Deployment and migration procedure

No deployment was performed by this change. Local Compose is not a production deployment. Supply reviewed secrets via your host's secret manager; runtime must satisfy `apps/api/src/config/env.ts`: production HTTPS origin, privileged MFA, enabled keyed Arcjet, SMTP authentication/TLS, private PostgreSQL and explicit proxy trust. External provider behavior remains unverified without credentials.

1. Take a protected PostgreSQL backup and verify a restore using the operations runbook.
2. Install locked dependencies, generate the client, build with the intended `API_INTERNAL_URL`: `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`, `pnpm db:generate`, `pnpm build`.
3. Run reviewed migrations once with a schema-owner `MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL`: `pnpm db:migrate`. Use least-privilege application and worker roles on the private DB. No automatic deploy/publish workflow is added.
4. Start supervised web and API processes: `pnpm --filter @nasj/web start`, `pnpm --filter @nasj/api start`. Start the built local consumer separately: `pnpm --filter @nasj/api worker --watch`.
5. Probe liveness and readiness and validate synthetic sign-in, scoped denial and worker status. Terminate gracefully; worker stops after its current bounded batch.

Migrations `202610200001_e16_reliability` and `202610200002_synthetic_commerce` add tables/type/indexes/constraints without rewriting existing data or backfilling events. The commerce migration preserves the synthetic-only boundary with database CHECK constraints and stores exact integer millimes. New API code requires it. Deploy schema before API/worker. Existing API versions ignore these new tables, permitting application rollback while preserving queue/outcome records. Stop worker before rollback. Do not drop tables or reset migrations as routine rollback: deleting command outcomes weakens retry guarantees. Review any destructive reverse migration separately with a verified backup. Database failure should fail readiness; liveness remains independent.

Hosting packaging, TLS/ingress, runtime credential provisioning, off-site backups, alert routing and signed release approval remain operator responsibilities. No real contracts or money movement are supported.


After additive migration `202610200003_commerce_projections`, run the separate worker for in-app notices and synthetic reporting. Backfill existing orders with `pnpm worker --rebuild-analytics` under trusted server configuration. Prior API/web builds can coexist with the additive tables; preserve them and receipts during rollback. Do not drop identity/commercial data. Configure owner-approved local backup targets and 7-day retention using the operations guide. Hosted storage/scheduling/alert destinations and physical-device verification are not supplied by this change.


===== docs\development\README.md =====

# Reproduce the website

Use Node 24 (validated with 24.20.0), pnpm 11.3.0, Docker Engine/Compose, and run from this repository root. No sibling repository is required.

```sh
pnpm install --frozen-lockfile
pnpm dev
```

`dev` creates/preserves private local environment, starts/reuses PostgreSQL 17.7 and Mailpit, builds contracts/generates Prisma, deploys migrations, seeds fictional accounts, and runs web/API at localhost:3000/3001. It refuses remote/production databases. Local credentials remain in ignored mode-0600 `.local/dev-credentials.json`; do not print or commit them. Mailpit is localhost:8026. Ctrl+C stops apps, preserving data. `pnpm services:stop` stops only this project's services. Never reset a shared database to fix migrations.

`.env.example` describes the server environment. `pnpm setup:local` preserves existing secrets. `pnpm db:migrate` uses deploy, `pnpm db:generate` generates the client, `pnpm db:seed` seeds local data. Website build ordering is contracts → API → web. The simulator has its own toolchain in the independent IoT repository. Use `pnpm worker --once`, `pnpm worker --watch`, or `pnpm worker --status` to consume/inspect metadata events in the configured database. The worker is an explicit separate process and does not send external messages.

Run `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm test:integration`, `pnpm test:e2e`, `pnpm audit --audit-level=high`, `pnpm build`. Browser tests need Chromium (`pnpm exec playwright install chromium`); `/usr/bin/chromium` is used when installed. Integration/browser tests allocate their own disposable containers and never read local database credentials for test writes. A restore drill runs within the integration suite.

Troubleshooting: verify `docker --context default info`, ports 3000/3001/5442/1026/8026, Node/pnpm versions and the browser Origin (localhost differs from 127.0.0.1). Rebuild after changing `API_INTERNAL_URL`; it is compiled into the Next rewrite. If browser tests regenerate next-env paths for `.next-e2e`, normal `pnpm build` restores the normal output paths.


## Run the synthetic commercial journeys

After the existing local setup, sign in with the private local fictional personas and open the Commerce navigation. Buyers need BUYER in an approved BUYER_BUSINESS organization. Production, QA, finance and logistics need their explicit role in the assigned approved INTERNAL organization. The seeded internal manager can assign missing synthetic staff roles in organization settings; no global ADMIN bypass is provided. Artisans choose their own craft and PIECES capacity window in `/artisan/profile`/`/artisan/capacity`; the window must cover the RFQ deadline. Future windows can be reserved. The seeded demo craft is DEMO — Traditional embroidery, not the reference weaving skill used in automated tests.

Buyer: save/reopen/edit a draft, submit it, then accept the exact unexpired quote. Operator: review/quote, schedule and progress a **simulated buyer receipt**, confirm funding, enter planning, issue immutable artisan offers. Artisan: review every term, accept or decline freely, then start material-ready work and report cumulative totals. Production releases accepted assignments; QA starts inspection, reconciles approved + rejected + pending, records rework or approval; logistics records synthetic shipment/delivery; buyer accepts receipt. Finance separately reconciles QA-earned artisan payouts before order settlement and records a synthetic materials/returns disposition before closure. See [the state and reconciliation rules](../architecture/commerce.md).

No real transaction occurs. Do not interpret an operator-entered material attestation or simulated payment label as observed physical/financial evidence. Commercial records have no delete/reset endpoint; use a fresh disposable database for repeatable tests, preserve local history, and never run test-reset/restore helpers against shared or production data.


Run `pnpm demo` from the separate `iot/simulator` directory for the accelerated fixed local device fixture. Website commands do not run or require it. Edit fixture values or inject a new DeviceAdapter when the device arrives; keep SIMULATED labels until physical verification. `pnpm worker --watch` is required for commerce reports/inbox; `pnpm worker --rebuild-analytics` safely backfills projections. `pnpm ops:backup` is explicit operator tooling requiring private key/storage configuration; see operations before use.


`pnpm verify:clean` verifies the current source in a fresh private temporary checkout: ordinary frozen install, setup, client generation, lint/types/unit/integration/browser tests, audit and production build. It excludes ignored files and secrets, creates disposable databases and uses test ports 3100/3101. Logs and per-command outcomes are written to ignored `.local/clean-verification`; the temporary checkout is removed. The checkout lives in the user's cache directory so pnpm uses its ordinary existing package store; integrity/security checks are not bypassed. This is a fresh source/dependency installation, not a claim of an empty package cache. It preserves the unrelated service on port 3000 and the developer database.

For approved local-demo backup/health scheduling and private alerts, use `pnpm ops:setup --prepare` then `--enable`; see [operations](../operations/README.md). Hardware and simulator communication remain outside website commands.

# Final local E16 verification — 2026-10-20

`clean-summary.json` records ten successful commands from the final fresh-source checkout: ordinary frozen install, setup, generation, lint/types, 46 website unit tests, 58 disposable integration scenarios, 15 browser cases, audit and production build. The normal verified pnpm package store was reused, not an empty cache. Network retry settings were tuned for this host's intermittent registry timeouts; no security/integrity checks were disabled. Earlier transient failed attempts remain historical and were not counted as passes.

The simulator is solely in IoT; `iot.log` records its own frozen install/audit/lint/types/12 tests/build/demo. Local user units were actually prepared, validated and enabled; local backup/configuration, seed/migration and outage/recovery observations are recorded without retaining secret values. Keys, plaintext configuration, archives, credential manifests and private application logs are excluded from evidence.

Physical device verification is deferred. Hosted deployment was excluded by the user. Current source publication still requires explicit authorization; the earlier hosted baseline run is distinct evidence.

===== docs\engineering\evidence\simulator-move\README.md =====

# Simulator relocation verification — 2026-10-20

Historical relocation-stage observations. Final normal fresh-install and hosted verification supersede these installation/publication limits; see `../../E16_TEST_RESULTS.md`.

The simulator was moved from the website workspace to the independent `iot/simulator` project at the user’s request. Website scripts and CI no longer build/run/test it; its old cross-repository integration scenario was removed. Communication remains deferred.

Executed: website lint/typecheck/production build and 42 unit tests plus 58 disposable integration scenarios; independent IoT offline frozen install/lint/typecheck, 12 tests, build and demo. Logs are retained here. Website dependency resolutions did not change. pnpm warns that installed workspace metadata still contains the removed package; local website checks used the existing installed toolchain with `pnpm_config_verify_deps_before_run=warn`. This warning does not skip test or compilation checks. The simulator installed and executed its own pinned tools successfully without any website reference.

Pre-move 54 combined-unit/59 integration/15 browser evidence stays in `../followup/`. No browser production source was changed for this relocation. IoT CI is configured locally and has not been published or run remotely. No environment credentials, archives or node_modules are retained in this evidence directory.

===== docs\engineering\E02_CATALOG_REPORT.md =====

# E02-01 / #31 — Buyer craft and example catalog

Implementation and local verification: 2026-10-20. Branch: `epic/e02-buyer-procurement-and-rfq-catalog`. This report covers [#31](https://github.com/wie-challenge/website/issues/31), not the complete E02 epic. Prerequisite #30 was confirmed closed. Issue closure and merge remain review actions.

## Result

Signed-in users can browse `/commerce/catalog` and filter active crafts. Four version-1 fictional examples show specifications, piece units, indicative day ranges and their planning assumptions. The runner and basket have original local SVG illustrations; embroidery demonstrates missing-image fallback, pottery is explicitly unavailable, and the reference “Other traditional crafts” category has no examples. A network image failure also falls back to readable specification text.

Eligible examples link to `/commerce/buyer?example=…`. The existing buyer workspace resolves the ID from the current server catalog before showing a prefilled request. Specifications remain editable. Quantity, destination and future deadline start blank and require buyer confirmation. Invalid or unavailable links display an actionable error and no creation form. Existing organization, session, CSRF, version and replay boundaries remain authoritative.

`GET /api/v1/commerce/catalog` returns at most 100 active crafts with a shared buyer-safe projection. It contains no organization procurement records, artisan identities, individual capacity, stock, prices or verified supply. `POST /api/v1/commerce/rfqs` validates optional `catalogExampleId` against its current active craft and fixture availability. It fingerprints that selection with the normal request, and persists only the buyer-confirmed RFQ fields. This initial example link is not approved-SKU lineage, a reservation, a quote, a stock check or a real contract. No migration, runtime dependency, network image provider or device integration was added.

## Acceptance mapping

| Original criterion | Implemented evidence |
|---|---|
| Categories display specifications, indicative lead-time ranges and demo labels. | Active-craft projection, category descriptions, four labelled examples and explicit fixture assumptions. API scenario and both viewport journeys. |
| List craft categories and examples with images, units and specification summaries. | Responsive category grid, original illustrated runner/basket, piece units and specification summaries. Browser checks assert a loaded image, filter and RFQ prefill. |
| Show indicative lead-time ranges and assumptions without promising unverified supply. | Per-example day ranges state fictional 10-piece planning assumptions and require capacity/material/shipping/date reassessment. No inventory, price or promise is projected. |
| Identify synthetic and unavailable products visibly. | Page disclosure plus each card's synthetic/illustrative or unavailable label; unavailable cards have no RFQ link. API rejects forged/unavailable/mismatched selections with no draft/event mutation. |
| Handle empty categories and missing images and link products into the RFQ form. | Empty category/catalog states; null-image and failed-image fallback; mobile/desktop keyboard link into the existing form, confirmed required fields, editable persisted draft and no order. |

## Verification

Final local checks: lint and type checks; 46 unit tests; 61 disposable PostgreSQL/Nest integration scenarios; 18 optimized Chromium cases; dependency audit; production build. The new catalog contributes three API scenarios and three browser cases. Its five main-content axe checkpoints have zero violations, alongside the retained 15 commerce checkpoints. Browser viewports are 360×800 and 1280×900; overflow and keyboard activation are asserted. The full browser run retains the existing slow-mobile commerce, identity/MFA and failure cases. This is scoped automated evidence, not general accessibility certification.

The API checks exercise real authenticated routes, empty active-craft projection, deactivation, foreign-organization write denial, strict schemas, altered/unknown/unavailable example IDs, replay/conflict and atomic failure. Browser loading/503/retry/empty-response checks use controlled routes; failed image requests are actually aborted. All test database writes use disposable containers; developer data is preserved. Screenshots `.local/catalog-{mobile,desktop}.png` and the detailed Playwright report are ignored locally and included in the existing three-day CI artifact. Safe aggregate results are committed in `evidence/e02-catalog/local-summary.json`; hosted status is provided by the feature pull request's checks.

An initial integration failure exposed the pre-existing operations CLI test's assumption that port 3001 was down. It now owns a temporary 503 endpoint, and the integration suite passed with the real developer API still running. Initial browser runs caught test-locator mismatches for wrapped selects/prefilled textareas and Next's separate route announcer; role/name queries and main-region alert scopes corrected those tests. The passing final results supersede those interrupted debugging runs.

## Review and remaining scope

Review covered the shared projection, active-craft/example validation, optional create field omission before Prisma persistence, unchanged edit schema, command fingerprint, query-string resolution, image origins and test isolation. No blocking issue remains in that inspected scope. The PR is ready for review after its checks pass; this report does not close an issue or merge the branch.

E02 #33 still needs its own complete draft/revision/field-error acceptance review after #31 is reviewed and accepted. Attachments, attributable timeline, revisions/clarifications, sample sign-off, discussions, immutable procurement documents and approved-SKU reorder are separate stories with the kickoff's dependency gates. E20 owns approved live SKU/version lineage. Physical #197 remains open and independent; all examples and simulator values remain synthetic.


===== docs\engineering\E02_COMPLETION_AUDIT.md =====

# E02 completion audit — 2026-10-21

**Historical pre-implementation audit.** See [the procurement delivery report](E02_PROCUREMENT_DELIVERY.md) for the subsequently implemented local-demo workflows and final verification. The full live-pilot dependency gates remain separate.

**At the time of this audit, E02 was not complete.** This audit compares the nine canonical stories and their expanded acceptance criteria in `docs/NASJ_FINAL_GitHub_Issues.csv` (documentation repository) with the API, database, UI and executed tests. The epic [#3](https://github.com/wie-challenge/website/issues/3) remains open. The canonical backlog is unchanged.

The catalog implementation was reviewed and merged through [PR #215](https://github.com/wie-challenge/website/pull/215), merge commit `823113b549b8603ddbaf2da653f5fa9240c8b3b2`. Its hosted Architecture and security checks passed. All nine story issues were open at audit time; an open issue and implemented software are distinct statuses.

===== docs\engineering\E02_PROCUREMENT_DELIVERY.md =====

# E02 procurement delivery — 2026-10-21

Branch: `epic/e02-procurement-completion`. This delivery implements the nine E02 buyer stories in the **local synthetic demonstration**, building on the merged category/example catalog. It does not authorize a live commercial pilot or close the E03/E09/E10/E20 upstream epics. Hosted checks and merge for this branch have not been performed.

## Buyer and operator workflows

Open `/procurement` after signing in. Buyers see their company requests; assigned NASJ operators see submitted requests for their assigned buyer accounts. Existing legacy internal finance actors retain the explicitly scoped synthetic regression workflow. Pending/suspended affiliations and revoked assignments are checked on every API request. Platform administrators receive no implicit commercial access.

1. Create and reopen an editable draft with specifications, design requirements, integer piece quantity and a future delivery deadline/destination. Confirm the NASJ team. Field errors appear beside the relevant labelled control. Submit the exact version once; retries reuse a scoped command key.
2. In References, select PNG/JPEG/WebP files, preview them, upload and remove draft references. There are at most five images, 256 KiB each and 16 megapixels. The server fully decodes and re-encodes each image as WebP, strips metadata and stores bytes privately in PostgreSQL. Reads require a current participant session plus a 60-second session-bound signed token. No public storage URL is created.
3. Follow the persisted Activity timeline and paginated specification Revisions. Events have stable IDs, timestamps and safe actor labels. Revisions retain author, reason, predecessor and full specification/attachment/clarification snapshots. Earlier history is never fabricated for legacy records.
4. Assigned operators start review and ask feasibility questions. Buyers answer with attributed immutable answers; answers become a new terms revision. Revisions and answers invalidate affected quotes and sample approval. Accepted obligations reject direct edits and require the separate approved amendment process.
5. Operators publish exact-version sample evidence and acceptance criteria. Explicitly authorized buyer signatories approve, reject or request changes with comments and time. A replacement sample needs a new decision. Managed full-production release checks the latest sample/specification approval; replacing a sample after production has progressed requires an amendment.
6. Operators issue a versioned quotation after recording current price, capacity and material review references and a synthetic tax-policy/rate snapshot. A buyer with explicit approval authority accepts a current unexpired exact quote. Acceptance, order and immutable contract snapshot are committed together. Stale, cross-company, superseded and duplicate commands cannot create another order.
7. Discuss the request/order with attributed plain-text messages. Internal operator notes stay outside buyer/coordinator threads and buyer activity. Assigned coordinators can access `/procurement/discussions` only for accepted orders involving a currently assigned, managed and authorized participant; this grants no prices, private notes or documents. React renders message text without HTML execution.
8. Download immutable numbered quote, contract, synthetic invoice and delivery-record JSON versions from `/procurement/documents`. Every download rechecks access; old quote versions are marked superseded. Delivery documents require persisted delivery evidence. Invoices copy accepted exact terms rather than current editable configuration. Individual artisan payment statements are never included.
9. Publish reusable approved product versions only after current sample approval and exact quotation acceptance. Record compatible materials and observed lead-time count/context. Buyers use `/procurement/products` to confirm a new quantity, destination and deadline; a reorder copies versioned specification and source lineage into a new draft, carrying no quote, acceptance, payment, order or sample approval. Discontinued/superseded products cannot be reordered or newly quoted. Existing obligations remain unchanged.

## Architecture and migration

The module reuses Better Auth, User, Organization/member grants, CommercialRfq/Order, IAM transactions, scoped idempotency, audit/outbox and the existing shadcn shell. New contracts are in `packages/contracts/src/procurement.ts`; authenticated endpoints are under `/api/v1/procurement`. Existing synthetic commerce endpoints remain compatible, while managed quotations must use the versioned acceptance path.

Migration `20261021030000_buyer_procurement` is additive and transactional. Eleven related tables hold revisions, activity, attachments, clarifications, discussions, samples/decisions, quotes/acceptance, approved product versions and documents. Foreign keys retain existing actors and obligations. Database triggers reject updates/deletes to immutable evidence; partial legacy history remains explicitly unavailable. Existing RFQs default to `procurementManaged=false`, preserving earlier simulator fixtures. The full encrypted backup/restore test includes all 51 application tables.

The local migration was applied only after an encrypted backup. Before/after row hashes are identical for **6 User, 6 Account and 2 Session records**. Private backups, identities and raw logs stay ignored under `.local`; no credentials are included in this document.

## Verification

Final local regression: **49 unit tests, 93 PostgreSQL integration scenarios, 25 browser tests**, with zero skipped/flaky/unexpected cases. The browser report includes **41 axe checkpoints with zero violations**. Lint/type checks, dependency audit and the production build passed. Prisma validation passed and the read-only database/schema diff is empty. Screenshot review led to a final navigation-spacing adjustment; all three affected procurement browser cases passed again after that adjustment. A frozen offline install also passed, and the existing local buyer account successfully opened `/procurement`. Safe aggregate evidence is in `evidence/e02-procurement/local-summary.json`.

Commands: `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm test:integration`, `pnpm test:e2e`, `pnpm audit --audit-level=high`, `pnpm build`, Prisma schema validation and read-only database/schema comparison. Raw evidence is private under `.local/e02/` and `.local/e2e-report.json`.

## Release boundary and remaining upstream work

This delivers synthetic buyer-facing workflows. Sample evidence/review references are recorded, not independently verified physical production. The full paid sample-offer, labor/material tracking and payable workflow remains E20-02. Approved-product lead-time observations require real verification before live publication. Price/capacity/material review references do not reserve capacity or establish material supply. The finance/logistics source records are local simulations: documents visibly say they are not tax or legal documents, and delivery records do not implement the full shortage/dispute/receipt domain. Live accounting/tax policy, controlled corrections/credits, approved contracts/amendments and verified provider reconciliation remain E03/E09/E10 prerequisites for a commercial pilot. Real payouts remain disabled. Physical wearable #197 remains pending hardware.

No canonical backlog IDs are rewritten and no issue is automatically closed. The existing `E02_COMPLETION_AUDIT.md` records the earlier pre-implementation gap assessment; this report supersedes its implementation-status findings for the local-demo slice after final verification.

## Architecture and contracts

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Web[Next.js commerce workspace] --> API[Nest session, strict input, tenant/resource roles]
  API --> TX[Atomic command, outcome, audit, metadata event]
  TX --> Source[(Authoritative synthetic PostgreSQL ledgers)]
  Source --> Worker[Separate bounded outbox worker]
  Worker --> Derived[(Projection, scoped notice, unique receipt)]
  Derived --> API
  Rules[Pure shared state, TND, quantity and metric rules] --> API
  Rules --> Worker
  Device[Independent fixed local wearable simulator] --> Summary[Private in-memory weekly summary]
```

No arrow connects personal wearable data to commerce. The worker reuses existing durable events rather than introducing a separate broker. API and workers share a fixed lock order for consistent prototype snapshots; throughput at commercial growth scale is not claimed. Local effects are atomic and deduplicated under at-least-once execution. Invitation/support SMTP remains a separate existing integration and is not called in a consumer transaction.

Derived reports carry SYNTHETIC/SIMULATED provenance, registry version, UTC order-lifetime period, asOf and pending/stale status. Produced, submitted, approved, shipped, received and accepted quantities retain requested denominators; zero denominator produces null rate. Earned/paid/outstanding and scheduled buyer/artisan amounts use exact millime strings and separate ledgers. Actual cost/hours/verified bank settlement have no supported source, so remain null with unavailable coverage. Reports are purpose/role scoped; a whole-order report is not available to an artisan.

Migration `202610200003_commerce_projections` is additive. Apply with the documented deploy command, run the worker, optionally backfill under trusted server configuration. Older compatible API/web versions can coexist with the new tables; preserve identity, ledger, outcomes, receipts and audit history during rollback.

The user explicitly authorized pushing both feature branches; no GitHub issues, parent epic, production data or live financial state were changed.

Private allowlisted local alert/status files replace any need for an unspecified external alert destination. An actual service backup succeeded, an intentional API outage produced API_NOT_READY, and starting the existing compiled API made the same operational check healthy. The temporary API was stopped afterward; no unrelated server on port 3000 was replaced. Local PostgreSQL network attachment and additive migrations were repaired/applied without resetting data or credentials.

`pnpm verify:clean` now executes the ordinary frozen install/setup/generate/static/unit/integration/browser/audit/build pipeline in a private fresh source checkout with disposable services and no ignored secrets. It uses the ordinary pnpm store and does not claim an empty package cache. Current evidence is under `evidence/final-local/`; earlier failed network/cache attempts are historical. A strict-package-resolution health bootstrap defect found during actual execution was fixed and covered in the CLI integration test. Website has 46 unit tests and 58 integration scenarios; IoT owns and separately verifies its 12 simulator tests. Physical-device observations remain deferred as agreed. Hosted deployment/off-site storage are outside the selected scope, and both feature branches have been pushed with explicit user authorization.

## Cross-cutting findings

- No monetary or commercial mutation exists, so exact money primitives cannot honestly be described as integrated settlement processing.
- Individual wearable fields are absent and strict schemas reject additional fields. Existing arbitrary text fields are not a semantic sensitive-data detector; avoid copying snapshots/text into events or analytics.
- IAM uses two global advisory locks: correct serialization at foundation scale, potential throughput bottleneck at growth scale. Preserve lock order in new transactions.
- Audit and resource permissions must be rechecked before returning idempotent outcomes; session/key possession alone is insufficient.
- Existing local Compose is not production infrastructure. Real provider checks, off-site retention, alert routing, hardware behavior and complete commerce acceptance remain release risks.
- No production writes, money movement, issue status changes, pushes or deployments are authorized.


## Follow-up disposition

This document preserves the initial repository audit. The user subsequently requested completion of #32/#88/#195. The explicit commerce states/rules in the product specification were sufficient to implement a bounded synthetic vertical workflow without claiming full upstream epics. The current implementation and verified status are in E16_TARGET_STORIES_REPORT.md and the updated acceptance matrix; statements above that commerce did not yet exist describe the baseline only.

| ETL isolation | Replay/backfill produce stable aggregates with unchanged source ledger; explicit source provenance/coverage and scope | PASS; no cost/time/verified-bank source invented, no wearable dataset accepted |
| Logging | Actual Pino sink excludes secret/body/cookie/authorization/signal sentinels while retaining correlation/duration | PASS tested structured paths; callers still must never put secrets in message text/unreviewed keys |
| Backup | Actual AES-GCM CLI database/private-configuration dump/decrypt/restore, legacy compatibility, wrong-key/tamper failure, private owner/permissions, no overwrite/symlink and seven-day pruning | PASS local/disposable; off-host storage/key escrow and production cutover unverified |
| Operations | Safe liveness/readiness, bounded DB acquisition, lag/failure alerts and approved 24-hour backup freshness | PASS local alert codes; daily backup/five-minute conditional health user timers and private allowlisted alert log configured/tested; no external paging |
| Wearable separation | Twelve simulator tests; fetch/TCP-denied lifecycle makes zero attempts; actual standalone process leaves capacity/order/event ledgers unchanged | PASS software simulation; no physical packet-capture or motor/accuracy claim |
| Supply chain | Current ordinary frozen fresh-source install and both website/IoT dependency audits executed successfully | PASS, no known vulnerabilities reported; dependency resolutions unchanged |

No confirmed unresolved cross-tenant/replay/ledger defect was found in the executed scope. Residual risks: personal IDs in restricted logs/queue/inbox require retention governance; shared locks deliberately serialize prototype throughput; temporary browser retry keys do not survive reload; restore can resurrect historical sessions requiring revocation; backups have a 64 MiB local-demo limit; hosted secret/storage/alert/provider controls and physical privacy checks need separate verification. Absence of a finding in these tests is not a blanket penetration-test/production certification.


Final local verification fixes strict pnpm health-CLI dependency resolution through an API-owned entrypoint. Scheduler subprocess output is reduced to fixed allowlisted codes; malformed/secret-bearing output is never copied to local alerts. Private status/alert files and timer command paths are tested, and actual systemd units validated/installed. A real backup and intentional API outage/recovery were observed. No production cutover, external message or device transport was introduced.

===== docs\foundation\DELIVERY_REPORT.md =====

# Revised foundation delivery — 2026-10-21

Implementation branch: `foundation/revised-role-model` in the website and documentation repositories. The existing Better Auth application and the shadcn UI work are preserved. No new application, authentication provider or duplicate administrator system was created. The completed foundation and UI changes are being submitted for hosted verification and merge; local verification is recorded below.

## Architecture and authorization

Four operational personas are resolved from the existing account and scoped memberships: PLATFORM_ADMIN (existing ADMIN), NASJ_OPERATOR, BUYER_REPRESENTATIVE and ASSOCIATION_COORDINATOR. ARTISAN is a participant with an optional verified account link. USER remains an ordinary platform account. Existing business-role enum values remain historical compatibility values; new assignments use the revised personas.

The existing Organization names BUYER_BUSINESS, ASSOCIATION and INTERNAL remain, with PARTNER_COOPERATIVE added. ASSOCIATION and INTERNAL correspond to PARTNER_ASSOCIATION and NASJ_INTERNAL in the business terminology.

The action catalog and organization-specific permission mapping are in `packages/contracts/src/permissions.ts`. AccessService/PolicyService enforce current account, role, permission and organization scope. Registry operations additionally require a single approved active affiliation, explicit participant assignment and the appropriate current authorization evidence. Governance checks existing ADMIN status and privileged MFA. Ordinary non-manager buyer representatives retain the existing non-privileged MFA treatment. Grants cannot turn buyer permissions into internal financial authority.

| Persona | Working foundation functions | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Administrator | Existing accounts/approval/audit/privacy controls; personnel invitation; coordinator status/transfer; participant reassignment, transfer and reviewed account link; authorization policies; independent concerns; permission diagnostics and explicit grants | No implicit private artisan registry or operational/financial membership |
| Internal operator | Assigned buyer and partner overview, real participant counts, scoped audit activity, minimal participant-reference duplicate investigation and reviewed duplicate tickets | Approved INTERNAL membership and explicit assigned-account scope; no unrelated contacts or individual payout information |
| Buyer representative | Own company/representative settings and invitations, approval status, existing synthetic RFQ interface | Purchasing can be independently removed/restored; exact quotation approval requires a separately audited grant; company ownership and active approval remain mandatory |
| Association coordinator | Assigned registry, no-account onboarding, profile/skills/availability, reviewed authorization history, worker-declared capacity and paginated histories | One approved active partner affiliation; no automatic access to other coordinators' private participant records |

Permissions for future pricing, assisted offers, production, logistics and finance are defined. Those commercial modules are not presented as functional new operator screens. Existing labelled synthetic commerce remains available to its authorized legacy actors, with new representative purchasing/approval restrictions enforced on the backend. Real payouts are disabled; initiation and approval grants cannot coexist for the same person. A future real-payout service must also enforce independent initiating/approving actors per immutable transaction, even after role changes.

## Database and preservation

Modified existing models: OrganizationType and BusinessRole enums, OrganizationMember (database-maintained coordinator marker and grant relationship), ArtisanProfile (nullable unique user, creator, participant status and registry history), CapacityDeclaration (assisted evidence reference), and explicit relation mappings on User/Organization. Two existing commerce projection relations now explicitly describe their existing PostgreSQL NO ACTION update behavior, eliminating schema drift without changing their database constraints.

Seven tables were added: MembershipPermission, ArtisanManagement, ArtisanAssignment, AuthorizationPolicy, OnboardingAuthorization, OperatorAssignment and ParticipantConcern. Existing organization/member/invitation, skills, capacity, consent, audit/outbox, Better Auth and commercial tables were reused.

Migrations:

- `20261021010000_revised_foundation`: transactional additive schema changes, foreign keys, history, account-optional profiles, conflict checks and data backfill. It stops with reference IDs if existing coordinators or artisans have conflicting active affiliations. It retains existing buyer approval as explicit authority and does not fabricate authorization evidence or coordinator assignments.
- `20261021020000_buyer_purchasing_authority`: additive enabled/disabled overrides for scoped purchasing/negotiation and explicit approval authority, retaining existing grants as enabled.

PostgreSQL partial unique indexes enforce one active coordinator affiliation, one active artisan managing relationship, one active responsible assignment and one active legacy artisan association. A trigger derives the coordinator marker from MembershipRole, so a client-supplied marker cannot bypass uniqueness. IAM transactions serialize validation and mutation; database constraints also reject concurrent direct writes. Actor/organization/participant foreign keys use retained identities with restricted deletion.

Local preflight found no conflicting affiliations. Encrypted backups were created before the local changes. Hash comparisons of every User, Account and Session row were identical before and after both migrations: **6 users, 6 credential records and 2 sessions preserved**. No real credentials are included in this report. A read-only Prisma database-to-schema diff is empty.

The conflict/upgrade test verifies migration rollback on duplicate coordinator and artisan affiliations, explicit conflict resolution in the disposable fixture, retained identity/history rows and preserved legacy approval grants. The existing full encrypted backup/restore drill now covers all 40 application tables.

## Backend interfaces

All authenticated mutations retain session-bound CSRF, strict input validation, transactional audit/outbox and current account checks. Collections use pagination; registry detail includes bounded recent history and separate paginated history endpoints. Safe projections omit unrelated personal/financial information.

| Interface | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/v1/me/context` | Own personas, scoped permissions and landing path |
| Existing `/api/v1/organizations`, organization settings/member/invitation and admin approval routes | Reused onboarding, company representatives and governance; admin organization listing adds a type filter |
| `PUT /api/v1/organizations/:id/members/:memberId/permissions` | Scoped purchasing/negotiation, buyer approval or explicit internal payout authority; reasons audited |
| `GET /api/v1/associations/me` and `/coordinators` | Resolve approved active association and its coordinator directory |
| `GET/POST /api/v1/associations/me/artisans` | Assigned list and authorized no-account onboarding |
| `GET/PATCH /api/v1/associations/me/artisans/:id` | Assigned participant detail/profile changes |
| `PUT .../:id/skills`, `POST .../:id/capacity` | Validated skills and separately authorized worker capacity declarations |
| `POST .../:id/authorization`, `POST .../:id/authorization/:evidenceId/withdraw` | Reviewed evidence and withdrawal, preserving history |
| `GET .../:id/capacity`, `/authorization`, `/assignments` | Paginated authorized histories |
| `GET /api/v1/admin/coordinators`, `/operators`, `/access-report` | Affiliation/personnel listings and effective permission diagnostics |
| `POST /api/v1/admin/personnel/invite` | Administrator-only coordinator/operator invitations through the existing hashed-token invitation service |
| `PATCH /api/v1/admin/coordinators/:userId/status`, `POST .../:userId/transfer` | Scoped activation/suspension/revocation and audited transfer; ambiguous historical affiliation requests require an exact organization |
| `POST /api/v1/admin/artisans/:id/assignment`, `/transfer`, `/link-account` | Reviewed coordinator reassignment, association transfer and verified identity conversion |
| `POST /api/v1/admin/operator-assignments` | Grant/revoke assigned buyer or partner accounts |
| `GET /api/v1/operator/dashboard`, `GET /api/v1/operator/activity`, `GET /operator/organizations/:id/participants`, `POST .../:id/duplicate-reviews` | Actual assigned network overview and minimal duplicate support |
| `GET /api/v1/authorization-policies`, `POST /admin/authorization-policies`, `PATCH /admin/authorization-policies/:id` | Reviewed methods/version references and withdrawal |
| `POST /api/v1/participant-concerns` | Rate-limited no-login independent intake; generic response does not reveal participant existence |
| `GET /api/v1/admin/participant-concerns`, `PATCH /api/v1/admin/participant-concerns/:id` | Private administrator concern review; a participant's creator/assigned coordinator cannot independently review that participant's concern |

Worker authorization is policy/version/purpose/method/time/language/evidence based. Witnessed verbal records require a separate witness. Capacity needs a separate CAPACITY record plus current PARTICIPATION evidence. Historical accepted offers/batches are not removed by new declarations, pause, withdrawal or transfer. Private phone information is redacted when participation authorization is inactive. Account conversion uses a reviewed reference and a verified account ID, never name matching.

The ArtisanDecisionEvidence contract prepares voluntary accepted/declined offer decisions with exact terms version, recorder, confirmation evidence, authorization context and review/dispute status. It is not an implemented assisted production service.

## Frontend journeys

The preserved shadcn shell now follows the identity context, with role-specific work links and explicit denied states for unauthorized administration and commerce routes. Hidden navigation is supplemented by API authorization.

- `/dashboard`: onboarding/pending access; existing organization creation and verification journey.
- `/admin`, `/admin/users`, `/admin/organizations`, `/admin/coordinators`, `/admin/operators`, `/admin/authorizations`, `/admin/access`, `/admin/audit`, `/admin/privacy-requests`, `/admin/participant-concerns`: working governance and access management.
- `/buyer`, `/buyer/company`, `/buyer/representatives`: own-company links to profile, approval, membership, invitations and independent purchasing/approval controls.
- `/association`, `/association/coordinators`, `/association/artisans`, `/association/artisans/new`, `/association/artisans/:id`, `/association/artisans/:id/history`: assisted registry, editing, skills, declared capacity, evidence, withdrawal and paginated history.
- `/operator` and `/operator/partners/:id`: assigned account/network overview, safe scoped activity and limited duplicate review.
- `/participant-support`: an artisan or trusted helper can report a concern without authentication or a fabricated account.

Default sign-in (including MFA completion) resolves to the appropriate authorized workspace. Explicit safe profile/settings destinations still work. An unauthorized route displays Access denied instead of redirecting into another role's dashboard.
