The shared shadcn button now transitions colors only, so disabled opacity ends immediately when the button becomes actionable. The existing catalog axe checks exercise the affected reload path; no accessibility rule is disabled and no scan delay is added. Final hosted status is recorded by [PR #216](https://github.com/wie-challenge/website/pull/216).

## Operational limits and backlog

This is a local foundation, not a real commercial pilot approval. Actual legal review of policy/methods and witness/evidence verification remains an operational requirement; this software records review references rather than claiming their truth or providing an SMS verification service. Independent concerns need staffed review and an accessible offline contact channel. Duplicate review uses scoped name/region/reference matching, not universal identity deduplication. Retention and hosting/backup/security operations require a real deployment review. Automated axe checks do not establish full accessibility conformance.

Real payouts remain disabled. Provider integration, verified funds/settlement evidence, independent approval thresholds and transaction-level maker/checker controls remain future E10 work. Assisted offer/production execution is a future module, with the evidence and access contract prepared here. Physical wearable verification (#197) remains pending device availability; no wearable data grants production authority.

No canonical story or issue is automatically closed. The foundation slices of E01 identity/assistance, E04 participant registry/capacity, E14 governance and E16 boundaries/migration/regression work are implemented. Entire E04/E05/E06/E10 epics are not claimed complete. Hosted CI is a required merge check for this delivery; production deployment has not been verified.

The documentation repository contains the requested `role-model-decision.md` and `backlog-role-reconciliation.md`, with explicit proposed acceptance-criteria changes and dependencies for E01/E04/E05/E06/E10/E14/E16. The 192-story canonical backlog is unchanged. Recommended next work: E02 procurement/RFQ and E03 exact quotation/approval, followed by assisted E04/E05 decisions before production execution.

See [the local walkthrough](TRY_THE_FOUNDATION.md) for the role journeys.


Verified foundation acceptance criteria map to E01-02/03/04/05/06/10/11; E04-04/05/06/11; E14-01/02/05/07; and E16-02/03/05/07/08/09. This is criteria-level coverage, not an automatic whole-story closure: the proposed deltas identify where operational policy or future commercial functionality remains. No implemented foundation feature is marked complete based only on an unexecuted command. Hosted CI/deployment, actual policy/process review and physical-device checks remain unverified; full assisted offer execution and real finance are unimplemented future scope.


===== docs\foundation\ROLE_RESTRUCTURING_AUDIT.md =====

# Foundation role restructuring audit — 2026-10-21

The existing application uses Better Auth with persistent User, Account, Session and Verification records, USER/ADMIN platform status, scoped OrganizationMember/MembershipRole records, token-hashed invitations, serialised IAM transactions, consent/delegation and immutable audit events. These remain authoritative.

Findings: ArtisanProfile.userId is mandatory; coordinator memberships can span associations; buyer and internal financial roles use legacy role checks; association managers can assign coordinator access; navigation derives from the commercial demo rather than a central identity context. Historical consent records belong to authenticated users, so assisted participation evidence needs a participant-specific record. Existing association relationships and delegations must remain valid history.

Implementation boundaries: four operational personas layered on existing accounts; legacy enum values retained, with restricted organization-specific compatibility mappings. Explicit grants control buyer quotation approval and sensitive financial authority. The existing membership table represents coordinator affiliations; a database-maintained marker and partial unique index enforce one active coordinator affiliation per user, including concurrent writes. Separate managing affiliations and coordinator assignments preserve artisan management history without deleting existing consent-linked relationships.

Migration is additive. Conflicting coordinator memberships or managing artisan relationships must stop migration with a conflict report, never be silently reassigned. Existing authentication records and commercial references remain untouched. Real payout functionality remains disabled; only the existing labelled simulation remains. Assisted authorization policies require an administrator-recorded review reference; software does not assert legal approval on its own.


===== docs\foundation\TRY_THE_FOUNDATION.md =====

# Try the revised foundation locally

Open `http://localhost:3000`. Existing local accounts, credentials and sessions were preserved. Keep `.local/dev-credentials.json` private; no password changes are needed for this migration.

## Administrator

Sign in to `/admin`. Review/approve partner and buyer organizations in `/admin/organizations`; filter by organization type and record a decision reason. An organization can be created/submitted through the existing organization settings. INTERNAL organizations require administrator creation.

Use `/admin/coordinators` to invite verified personnel to approved associations/cooperatives, suspend or transfer affiliations, reassign participants, transfer managing associations with new evidence, or link a reviewed verified account to an existing participant. Invitations are emailed as single-use links, accepted with the exact invited email. A second active coordinator affiliation is rejected. Status changes identify the exact affiliation; ambiguous historical affiliation changes are rejected.

Use `/admin/operators` to invite internal personnel, manage their membership status and grant/revoke assigned buyer/partner accounts. Use the reference identifiers in account/access administration for these reviewed operations. The inviter's current authority is checked again when an invitation is accepted, including when a former administrator still has an organization-manager membership.

In `/admin/authorizations`, record a reviewed policy version, approved evidence methods and legal-review reference before real participant onboarding. For disposable demonstrations use only fictional participants and clearly synthetic references. Such references do not constitute legal approval for real participation. `/admin/access` shows effective permissions and membership references; `/admin/audit` and existing privacy controls remain available.

Review `/admin/participant-concerns` separately from the person responsible for the participant's disputed record. Self-review is rejected. Administrator status alone does not grant access to private participant operations or individual finances.

## Association coordinator

After approval and active affiliation, sign-in opens `/association`. Open Artisan registry → Add artisan. Enter the necessary name/region/language, skills, equipment/capabilities and availability, then record participation authorization. No participant email, password or smartphone is required. The association and responsible coordinator come from the authenticated context.

Evidence needs an active reviewed policy, an allowed method, date/time, language and external evidence reference. Documented verbal authorization also needs a separate witness reference. A checkbox alone is insufficient; the software records human evidence references rather than implementing SMS/document verification.

Open the participant record and record a separate CAPACITY authorization under “Record new worker authorization.” Then record the artisan's stated weekly quantity/unit and effective period using that declaration evidence. New capacity does not delete accepted work or history, and wearable fields are rejected. Use the history link to page through authorization, capacity and assignment records.

Other coordinators cannot view private fields without an explicit assignment. Affiliation suspension/revocation blocks access immediately. Withdrawing participation pauses assisted activity and redacts private phone information. Managing transfers retain history and end old assignments. Similar records require an assigned operator's independent duplicate-review reference.

## Buyer representative

Register and verify email, create a BUYER_BUSINESS and request approval through `/settings/organizations`. Pending accounts land at onboarding; approved representatives land at `/buyer`. Company links open the existing profile, approval, representative and invitation settings.

A company manager can invite more representatives without shared credentials. Member settings independently authorize/remove purchasing or negotiation, and grant/revoke final quotation approval. An approval-only representative can read company records and approve an authorized quotation while lacking permission to prepare/submit RFQs. API checks enforce these distinctions.

The existing craft catalog and synthetic buyer request flow remain available within company scope. Buyers cannot access internal operator, association or administrator workspaces, individual artisan payouts or internal financial administration.

## NASJ operator

After an administrator invitation is accepted, sign-in opens `/operator`. Only assigned approved buyer/partner accounts appear. Assigned-account activity exposes safe audit metadata; private snapshots and user-entered reasons are excluded. Partner review exposes minimal participant references and independent duplicate review, without contact or financial records.

Pricing, assisted offers, production and actual payments are explicitly upcoming for the new persona. The foundation does not pretend to implement a full new commercial workflow. Real payouts remain disabled.

## Participant without an account

Open `/participant-support`, or ask a trusted helper. Submit a participant/offer reference and a concern, with an optional safe contact method. The response does not reveal whether a reference exists and creates no fake User. NASJ administrators receive it independently of association operations. A real pilot must staff this review and supply accessible offline contact details during onboarding.

## Commands and migrations

From `website/`:

```bash
pnpm exec tsx --env-file=.env scripts/role-migration-preflight.ts
pnpm --filter @nasj/api exec prisma validate
pnpm lint
pnpm typecheck
pnpm test
pnpm test:integration
pnpm test:e2e
pnpm audit --audit-level=high
pnpm build
```

Preflight writes a private `.local/role-migration-preflight.json`. Review conflicts and legacy assignments, verify the intended datasource and take an encrypted backup before the normal `pnpm db:migrate` procedure. Never delete/reassign conflicting real records merely to satisfy an index. The current local migrations were already applied with encrypted backups and identical User/Account/Session row hashes.

See [the delivery report](DELIVERY_REPORT.md) for verification and limits. The documentation repository contains the proposed role-model decision and backlog reconciliation. The canonical backlog is unchanged; real payouts and physical-device verification remain pending their separate prerequisites.


===== docs\operations\README.md =====

# Operations, backup and recovery

API JSON logs contain random correlation IDs, normalized route labels, status and duration. Request bodies, raw URLs, credentials, cookies and wearable payloads are omitted/redacted. Actual Pino output is tested with sentinel secrets. IDs remain personal metadata: restrict log access. Worker logs expose event/correlation IDs, status, attempts, duration and fixed error codes, without exception text or free text from audits.

`GET /api/health/live` checks the process; `GET /api/health/ready` checks PostgreSQL and safely returns 503 when unavailable. PostgreSQL connection acquisition is bounded to five seconds. Readiness does not certify SMTP/Arcjet or a backup. `pnpm ops:check` probes local readiness with a three-second HTTP timeout, database/queue status, failed deliveries and lag over five minutes. A configured `BACKUP_DIRECTORY` also enables missing/stale (>24-hour) backup alerts; invalid/inaccessible backup storage emits BACKUP_UNAVAILABLE. Fixed JSON codes and nonzero exit support a supervisor. Local user timers and a private alert log are available below. No external paging integration is configured.

## Approved local-demo policy

On 2026-10-20 the user explicitly approved: **owner = project user; recovery point target = 24 hours; recovery time target = four hours; encrypted-backup retention = seven days**. These are reviewed targets for the local synthetic demo, not measured production guarantees. The local owner has enabled the daily backup and five-minute health timers described below; alerts stay in the private local log. Hosted/off-site storage, region, key escrow and production ownership remain outside the selected local-demo scope. A local disk alone does not protect against host loss.

The executable `pnpm ops:backup` runs PostgreSQL 17 `pg_dump -Fc` inside the selected Docker default-context container. Container authentication stays internal: no password or database URL in command arguments. The tool supports archives up to 64 MiB for this local demo and fails on larger dumps; use reviewed streaming/managed backups before larger deployment. It encrypts in memory using **AES-256-GCM**, random nonce and authenticated HCAB1 format, writes a new 0600 archive without overwrite/symlink following and requires a private owned directory and owned 0600, exactly 32-byte key file. Wrong keys/tampered envelopes fail authentication before any restore. No unencrypted archive or configuration copy is written by the backup command. Managed local backups include the private runtime `.env` (including authentication/encryption configuration) inside the authenticated encrypted payload; the backup encryption key itself remains separate. Old matching private archives are pruned only after a new backup succeeds; unrelated files are preserved. Root ignore rules exclude key/dump/encrypted archive artifacts.

Prepare private directories and a key outside Git (example path under ignored `.local` for the local demo). Back up the key separately under owner-controlled access; loss of the key makes restoration impossible. Do not print the key or upload archives/environment files in CI.

```sh
install -d -m 700 .local/backups .local/backup-keys
(umask 077; set -C; openssl rand 32 > .local/backup-keys/demo.key)
export BACKUP_CONTAINER=nasj-postgres-1
export BACKUP_DIRECTORY="$PWD/.local/backups"
export BACKUP_KEY_FILE="$PWD/.local/backup-keys/demo.key"
export BACKUP_DATABASE_USER=nasj
export BACKUP_DATABASE_NAME=nasj
export BACKUP_CONFIG_FILE="$PWD/.env"
pnpm ops:backup
pnpm ops:check
```

Choose the actual container/user/database from the local compose configuration; the example is not automatically executed. Generate the key once and preserve it; do not overwrite an existing recovery key. Success emits BACKUP_CREATED, filename, encrypted byte count, configurationIncluded flag, duration and number of expired archives removed. Failure emits only BACKUP_FAILED and a nonzero exit. Backup-age checks inspect private archive metadata, not decryptability or source integrity; periodic restores remain mandatory.

The real integration drill invokes this exact backup CLI against a newly created synthetic test container, decrypts/authenticates the payload, verifies private configuration byte-for-byte into the isolated test context, extracts a 0600 temporary database archive and restores using `pg_restore --clean --if-exists --exit-on-error` into a second disposable container and compares every public table's row count/content hash. This includes RFQs, orders, offers, batches, inspections, exact payment amounts, command outcomes, audits, notices, projections and receipts. Both containers/private files are removed in finally blocks. The destructive restore helper accepts only test-harness container names. It cannot accept a production restore URL. See the measured observations in `../engineering/E16_TEST_RESULTS.md`.

Production recovery requires an isolated target, protected decryption tooling/key access, disabled integrations and explicit cutover review. Do not restore over the working database. Check migration history, quantities, earned/paid/outstanding obligations and all row hashes. Historical identity backups can resurrect sessions/tokens: revoke/rotate before cutover. Preserve audit and deduplication history. A successful small local drill does not demonstrate hosted/off-site recovery or the approved four-hour target at production scale.

## Worker, analytics and replay

`pnpm worker --watch` runs committed local inbox delivery and synthetic analytics ETL. `--once` processes at most 50 events. `--status` reports counts, oldest pending age and up to 20 failed event IDs. Five failures enter FAILED with fixed LOCAL_CONSUMER_FAILED; retries use exponential delays. Investigate code/version/source first, then `pnpm worker --retry-failed EVENT_ID`. Queue access is trusted-server only; no public replay endpoint exists. Do not erase outcomes/receipts/queue rows as an operational remedy.

The prototype uses the existing database outbox for these justified workloads, without a broker. API commands and consumers acquire the same IAM locks in a fixed order; this intentionally serializes short prototype transactions to preserve consistent source snapshots. Row locks are the running state; no stale lease is needed. A killed process rolls back and releases its claim. Projection, notice and receipt effects commit atomically. Both failure-after-effects and actual SIGKILL/restart recovery are tested. This is at-least-once processing with durable local deduplication, not exactly-once external delivery or a demonstrated growth-scale throughput claim.

`pnpm worker --rebuild-analytics` recomputes order projections from authoritative synthetic rows and shipment/acceptance audit milestones, in cursor batches of 50 (maximum programmatic batch 100). It writes no commercial ledger or notices. Re-running is safe; metrics remain stable and asOf advances. Backfill failures exit nonzero; retry rebuild from the start safely. Normal event delivery carries persisted attempts/duration/failure/lag. Reports display stale/pending status for outstanding buyer-organization events. External email/invitation/support delivery remains separate from this database-local worker; do not call SMTP inside its transaction.

For incidents: correlate safe request/event IDs, inspect readiness/DB availability and migration state, check worker health/lag, repair the cause and selectively replay. On regression stop the worker and roll back to the previous compatible API/web build while preserving additive tables. For failed migration inspect `_prisma_migrations`, back up, repair and use reviewed resolve/deploy procedures. Never reset shared data. Hosted routing, off-site storage and provider outages need separate deployment verification.


## Local-demo schedule and alert destination

`pnpm ops:setup --prepare` validates the canonical local development configuration, preserves an existing private recovery key/configuration, and prepares/verifies user systemd units under ignored `.local/operations/units`. `pnpm ops:setup --enable` installs only NASJ-managed units in the current user's systemd directory and enables the timers; it refuses unmanaged replacements. `pnpm ops:setup --disable` disables those timers while preserving backup archives and keys. No system-wide services, external alert messages or lingering user session are configured.

The backup timer runs daily at midnight in the host timezone and catches missed runs when the user manager resumes. The health timer checks every five minutes while `.local/dev.lock` indicates the canonical `pnpm dev` session is active. It pauses while the application is intentionally stopped; stale locks after a crash still allow outage detection until the normal launcher cleans them up. The local host was configured and checked on 2026-10-20. The project's previously disconnected PostgreSQL container was reattached to its own existing Docker network; migrations were then applied without resetting its volume or credentials.

`pnpm ops:run backup` / `pnpm ops:run health` invokes the actual underlying commands with bounded timeouts. Only allowlisted result codes reach `.local/operations/{backup,health}.json`, a private 0600 latest-status file, and failures append to private `alerts.ndjson` (bounded to approximately 1 MiB). Raw child output, exception details and secrets are never copied to alerts. systemd also records service exit state. User-timer execution requires the machine and user manager to be running; the reviewed RPO/RTO remain targets, not guarantees while the host is off. Reprepare units after changing the Node installation/project location; the local units reference the current explicit executable and source paths.

```sh
pnpm ops:setup --prepare
pnpm ops:setup --enable
systemctl --user list-timers 'nasj-local-*'
pnpm ops:run backup
pnpm ops:run health
systemctl --user status nasj-local-backup.service nasj-local-health.service
pnpm ops:setup --disable
```

A real scheduled-service backup succeeded. An intentionally stopped API produced API_NOT_READY; starting the existing compiled API made the actual operational command return OPERATION_OK. The temporary API process was then stopped, and health monitoring is paused until the next canonical dev session. Tests also exercise malformed/secret-bearing child output filtering, private alert/status permissions and symlink rejection. `scripts/check-operations.ts` now boots its API-owned entrypoint so strict pnpm resolution finds reflect-metadata in its declared package.


Database-only legacy payloads remain readable. Current payload version 2 stores a bounded private configuration file together with the PostgreSQL custom dump, all authenticated/encrypted under HCAB1. Configuration inputs must be owned regular files with no symlink, private permissions and a maximum of 1 MiB; the total encrypted input remains limited to 64 MiB. `unpackDatabaseBackup(decryptBackup(...))` separates database and configuration for a reviewed isolated recovery. Never print recovered configuration or overwrite the active `.env`; stage it with 0600 permissions outside the live application and review target URLs/session rotation before cutover. No private-document/upload feature exists to back up; add any future required document store to the inventory. Preserve/recover the backup key separately.


===== docs\security\README.md =====

# Security model and residual risks

Nest independently enforces Better Auth sessions, active verified accounts, privileged MFA, CSRF, approved origin/JSON, strict Zod contracts, bounded lists and durable rate limits. Frontend roles/hidden buttons never grant access. Organization permissions derive from current membership/approval. Artisan assistance remains explicitly consent/scoped; global ADMIN alone does not grant organization or artisan access.

Commerce uses actual current BUYER membership in the owning approved buyer organization and specific operational roles in its assigned approved INTERNAL organization. Only the owning artisan accepts/declines or reports progress. QA cannot approve payments; buyers cannot read individual offers/payouts; artisans cannot read buyer quotes/receipts; unsubmitted RFQ drafts stay private. Client-substituted tenant/object/batch IDs do not bypass these checks. Six related tables enforce immutable synthetic provenance and bounded/reconciled rows. The API does not support live contracts or transfers.

Capacity and commerce command outcomes bind actor, resolved resource, operation and canonical payload. Commerce requires an idempotency key and optimistic version; current authorization/consent checks precede replay. Existing unkeyed capacity calls still intentionally create revisions. All commerce state/count/money decisions invoke pure rules inside the shared IAM transaction/lock order. State, audit, outcome and metadata event commit together. External invitation/support SMTP is not covered by the internal local receipt consumer guarantee.

Outbox events allow only IDs/types/actor/tenant/correlation/version/timestamps, with no snapshot/reason/specification/term/payment/sensor payload. IDs and private outcomes remain personal metadata requiring restricted access and retention review. There is no monitoring ingestion or commercial ETL. Strict schema rejection demonstrates explicit-field exclusion, not semantic detection of sensitive information entered into permitted free text. No medical efficacy or complete privacy-compliance claim is made.

Deployment still needs least-privilege DB grants, reviewed retention/outcome expiry, encrypted off-site backup storage, operator-approved RPO/RTO, ingress/TLS/proxy trust and hosted alert routing. Conservative prototype branches block unresolved disputes/amendments/partial-fulfillment remedies rather than erasing liabilities. No real bank/provider adapter, independent penetration test or complete accessibility certification is supplied. See the [security execution report](../engineering/E16_SECURITY_TEST_REPORT.md) and [commerce architecture](../architecture/commerce.md).


The commerce report and CSV endpoints recheck approved current resource memberships/roles inside the same IAM transaction as the read. Buyer output omits artisan private earnings; non-finance internal roles receive fulfillment only. Whole-order analytics is denied to artisans and unrelated buyers. Inbox scopes are derived from current memberships and artisan account identity, and revocation hides prior organization notices. No public rebuild/queue/backup route exists. CSV uses fixed names/enums and integers, avoiding untrusted spreadsheet formulas. Automated integration tests cover these reads, downloads and revocation.

Database-local consumers write derived projections/notices/receipts atomically; actual process termination and rollback/recovery are tested. No SMTP call occurs inside those transactions. The independent simulator has no API, database or network dependency; its fixture lifecycle makes zero attempted fetch/TCP calls and cannot alter commercial/capacity records. Physical network non-upload remains pending hardware. Backups use authenticated AES-256-GCM with private owned key/archive paths; tampering/permission/symlink/overwrite/retention failures and actual logger redaction are tested. Retain and recover encryption keys separately from archives.

===== docs\ui\README.md =====

# Minimal workspace UI

The workspace uses a neutral shadcn/ui theme with a teal accent, a desktop sidebar and a mobile navigation drawer. Work links follow the signed-in user's buyer, artisan and operator capabilities; administration appears only for administrators. API authorization remains authoritative.

Buyer requests, artisan production and operator review retain their existing commands. Request creation, planning assumptions, simulated payment records and notifications use expandable sections. Counts describe records returned in the current workspace, rather than organization-wide totals. The catalog keeps example and lead-time disclosures and the existing RFQ prefill flow.

Account settings use keyboard-accessible tabs for personal details, password and sessions, and account access. Existing authentication, CSRF handling, validation and session behavior remain in place. Demo payments and example catalog content remain explicitly labelled.

## Components and styling

Components in `apps/web/src/components/ui` are adapted from the official [shadcn/ui new-york-v4 registry](https://ui.shadcn.com/r/styles/new-york-v4/button.json). The upstream [MIT license](../../apps/web/src/components/ui/LICENSE) is included. Local changes give buttons an explicit keyboard outline, improve tab-label contrast and enlarge the sheet close control.

`apps/web/components.json` records the registry configuration. Tailwind CSS v4 runs through PostCSS; CSS variables in `apps/web/src/app/globals.css` define colors, spacing and radii. The stylesheet also maintains shared styles for existing organization, artisan and authentication screens. Dependencies are pinned in the workspace lockfile. Add components under `src/components/ui`, preserve the license and check keyboard behavior and contrast when adapting their styles.

## Verification

Run `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm test:integration`, `pnpm test:e2e`, `pnpm audit --audit-level=high` and `pnpm build` from the website repository.

Browser tests use disposable PostgreSQL data and synthetic identities. `tests/e2e/workspace-ui.spec.ts` checks capability-based navigation, active links, the request composer, keyboard account tabs and the mobile drawer's focus, Escape and navigation behavior at 360px. It also checks page overflow and runs axe on the full desktop workspace, mobile account, open drawer and mobile catalog. Existing catalog and commerce tests cover the buyer-to-artisan-to-operator journey with QA, shipment, simulated payment and reports.

Screenshots are written to ignored `.local/ui-*.png`, `.local/catalog-*.png` and `.local/commerce-*-operator.png`; structured browser results are in `.local/e2e-report.json`. CI collects these as short-lived verification artifacts. No real user credentials are included.

===== packages\contracts\src\commerce\contracts.ts =====

import { z } from 'zod';
import { parseTnd } from '../domain.js';
import { rfqStates, offerStates, batchStates, paymentStates, orderStates } from './domain.js';
const id = z.string().regex(/^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,128}$/);
const text = z.string().trim().min(2).max(2000);
const units = z.number().int().min(1).max(1000000);
const count = z.number().int().min(0).max(1000000);
const version = z.number().int().min(1);
const date = z.iso.datetime({ offset: true });
export const tndSchema = z.string().refine((value) => {
  try {
    parseTnd(value);
    return true;
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}, 'Use nonnegative TND with at most three decimal places within the supported limit.');
export const rfqCreateSchema = z
  .object({
    buyerOrganizationId: id,
    operatorOrganizationId: id,
    craftSkillId: id,
    title: text.max(120),
    specification: text,
    designRequirements: text,
    quantity: units,
    deliveryAt: date,
    deliveryLocation: text.max(200),
    provenance: z.literal('SYNTHETIC'),
    catalogExampleId: id.optional(),
  })
  .strict();
export const rfqEditSchema = rfqCreateSchema
  .omit({
    buyerOrganizationId: true,
    operatorOrganizationId: true,
    provenance: true,
    catalogExampleId: true,
  })
  .extend({ version })
  .strict();
export const rfqActionSchema = z.discriminatedUnion('next', [
  z
    .object({
      next: z.enum(['SUBMITTED', 'UNDER_REVIEW', 'ACCEPTED', 'DECLINED', 'EXPIRED']),
      version,
    })
    .strict(),
  z
    .object({ next: z.literal('QUOTED'), version, quoteTnd: tndSchema, quoteExpiresAt: date })
    .strict(),
]);
export const offerCreateSchema = z
  .object({
    orderId: id,
    capacityDeclarationId: id,
    quantity: units,
    unitPayTnd: tndSchema,
    estimatedHours: text.max(100),
    expiresAt: date,
    materials: text,
    reworkTerms: text,
    paymentConditions: text,
    provenance: z.literal('SYNTHETIC'),
  })
  .strict();
export const offerActionSchema = z.object({ next: z.enum(offerStates), version }).strict();
export const batchActionSchema = z
  .object({ next: z.enum(batchStates), version, reworkAccepted: z.literal(true).optional() })
  .strict();
export const progressSchema = z.object({ version, produced: count }).strict();
export const inspectionSchema = z
  .object({
    version,
    approved: count,
    rejected: count,
    pending: count,
    defectReason: z.string().trim().max(1000).default(''),
  })
  .strict()
  .refine((v) => v.rejected === 0 || v.defectReason.length >= 2, 'Explain rejected units.');
export const orderActionSchema = z
  .object({
    next: z.enum(orderStates),
    version,
    materialsResolved: z.literal(true).optional(),
    dispositionNote: z.string().trim().min(10).max(1000).optional(),
  })
  .strict()
  .refine(
    (v) => v.next !== 'CLOSED' || (v.materialsResolved && v.dispositionNote),
    'Confirm and describe the synthetic material disposition before closing.',
  );
export const paymentCreateSchema = z
  .object({
    orderId: id,
    batchId: id.optional(),
    kind: z.enum(['BUYER_RECEIPT', 'ARTISAN_PAYOUT']),
    amountTnd: tndSchema,
    provenance: z.literal('SYNTHETIC'),
  })
  .strict()
  .refine(
    (v) => (v.kind === 'ARTISAN_PAYOUT' ? Boolean(v.batchId) : !v.batchId),
    'Artisan payouts require a batch; buyer receipts must not select a batch.',
  );
export const paymentActionSchema = z
  .object({
    next: z.enum(paymentStates),
    version,
    evidenceType: z.literal('SIMULATED_SETTLEMENT').optional(),
  })
  .strict();
export type RfqCreate = z.infer<typeof rfqCreateSchema>;
export type RfqEdit = z.infer<typeof rfqEditSchema>;
export type RfqAction = z.infer<typeof rfqActionSchema>;
export type OfferCreate = z.infer<typeof offerCreateSchema>;
export type OfferAction = z.infer<typeof offerActionSchema>;
export type BatchAction = z.infer<typeof batchActionSchema>;
export type ProgressInput = z.infer<typeof progressSchema>;
export type InspectionInput = z.infer<typeof inspectionSchema>;
export type OrderAction = z.infer<typeof orderActionSchema>;
export type PaymentCreate = z.infer<typeof paymentCreateSchema>;
export type PaymentAction = z.infer<typeof paymentActionSchema>;
export type CommercialRfqView = {

export type CommercialOfferView = {

===== packages\contracts\src\commerce\domain.ts =====

import { MAX_TND_MILLIMES } from '../domain.js';

export class CommerceRuleError extends Error {
  constructor(
    readonly code: string,
    message: string,
  ) {
    super(message);
  }
}
export function requireRule(condition: unknown, code: string, message: string): asserts condition {
  if (!condition) throw new CommerceRuleError(code, message);
}
export const rfqStates = [
  'DRAFT',
  'SUBMITTED',
  'UNDER_REVIEW',
  'QUOTED',
  'ACCEPTED',
  'DECLINED',
  'EXPIRED',
] as const;
export const offerStates = ['PLANNED', 'OFFERED', 'ACCEPTED', 'DECLINED', 'EXPIRED'] as const;
export const batchStates = [
  'ACCEPTED',
  'MATERIAL_READY',
  'IN_PROGRESS',
  'SUBMITTED',
  'INSPECTION',
  'APPROVED',
  'REWORK_REQUESTED',
  'DISPUTED',
  'COMPLETED',
] as const;
export const paymentStates = [
  'SCHEDULED',
  'APPROVED',
  'INITIATED',
  'SETTLED',
  'FAILED',
  'CANCELLED',
  'DISPUTED',
] as const;
export const orderStates = [
  'APPROVED',
  'FUNDING_CONFIRMED',
  'PLANNING',
  'IN_PRODUCTION',
  'QUALITY_REVIEW',
  'READY_TO_SHIP',
  'IN_TRANSIT',
  'DELIVERED',
  'BUYER_ACCEPTED',
  'SETTLED',
  'CLOSED',
  'DISPUTED',
  'CANCELLED',
  'AMENDED',
] as const;
export type RfqState = (typeof rfqStates)[number];
export type OfferState = (typeof offerStates)[number];
export type BatchState = (typeof batchStates)[number];
export type PaymentState = (typeof paymentStates)[number];
export type OrderState = (typeof orderStates)[number];
export type CommerceRole =
  | 'BUYER'
  | 'ARTISAN'
  | 'PRODUCTION_MANAGER'
  | 'QUALITY_INSPECTOR'
  | 'FINANCE_MANAGER'
  | 'INVENTORY_LOGISTICS_COORDINATOR';
type Edge<S extends string> = readonly [S, S, readonly CommerceRole[]];
export const rfqEdges: readonly Edge<RfqState>[] = [
  ['DRAFT', 'SUBMITTED', ['BUYER']],
  ['SUBMITTED', 'UNDER_REVIEW', ['PRODUCTION_MANAGER']],
  ['UNDER_REVIEW', 'QUOTED', ['FINANCE_MANAGER']],
  ['QUOTED', 'ACCEPTED', ['BUYER']],
  ['QUOTED', 'DECLINED', ['BUYER']],
  ['QUOTED', 'EXPIRED', ['FINANCE_MANAGER']],
];
export const offerEdges: readonly Edge<OfferState>[] = [
  ['PLANNED', 'OFFERED', ['PRODUCTION_MANAGER']],
  ['OFFERED', 'ACCEPTED', ['ARTISAN']],
  ['OFFERED', 'DECLINED', ['ARTISAN']],
  ['OFFERED', 'EXPIRED', ['PRODUCTION_MANAGER']],
];
export const batchEdges: readonly Edge<BatchState>[] = [
  ['ACCEPTED', 'MATERIAL_READY', ['PRODUCTION_MANAGER']],
  ['MATERIAL_READY', 'IN_PROGRESS', ['ARTISAN']],
  ['IN_PROGRESS', 'SUBMITTED', ['ARTISAN']],
  ['SUBMITTED', 'INSPECTION', ['QUALITY_INSPECTOR']],
  ['INSPECTION', 'APPROVED', ['QUALITY_INSPECTOR']],
  ['INSPECTION', 'REWORK_REQUESTED', ['QUALITY_INSPECTOR']],
  ['INSPECTION', 'DISPUTED', ['ARTISAN', 'QUALITY_INSPECTOR']],
  ['REWORK_REQUESTED', 'IN_PROGRESS', ['ARTISAN']],
  ['REWORK_REQUESTED', 'DISPUTED', ['ARTISAN']],
  ['APPROVED', 'COMPLETED', ['PRODUCTION_MANAGER']],
];
export const paymentEdges: readonly Edge<PaymentState>[] = [
  ['SCHEDULED', 'APPROVED', ['FINANCE_MANAGER']],
  ['APPROVED', 'INITIATED', ['FINANCE_MANAGER']],
  ['INITIATED', 'SETTLED', ['FINANCE_MANAGER']],
  ['INITIATED', 'FAILED', ['FINANCE_MANAGER']],
  ['SCHEDULED', 'CANCELLED', ['FINANCE_MANAGER']],
  ['APPROVED', 'CANCELLED', ['FINANCE_MANAGER']],
  ['INITIATED', 'DISPUTED', ['FINANCE_MANAGER']],
];
export const orderEdges: readonly Edge<OrderState>[] = [
  ['APPROVED', 'FUNDING_CONFIRMED', ['FINANCE_MANAGER']],
  ['FUNDING_CONFIRMED', 'PLANNING', ['PRODUCTION_MANAGER']],
  ['PLANNING', 'IN_PRODUCTION', ['PRODUCTION_MANAGER']],
  ['IN_PRODUCTION', 'QUALITY_REVIEW', ['PRODUCTION_MANAGER']],
  ['QUALITY_REVIEW', 'READY_TO_SHIP', ['QUALITY_INSPECTOR']],
  ['READY_TO_SHIP', 'IN_TRANSIT', ['INVENTORY_LOGISTICS_COORDINATOR']],
  ['IN_TRANSIT', 'DELIVERED', ['INVENTORY_LOGISTICS_COORDINATOR']],
  ['DELIVERED', 'BUYER_ACCEPTED', ['BUYER']],
  ['BUYER_ACCEPTED', 'SETTLED', ['FINANCE_MANAGER']],
  ['SETTLED', 'CLOSED', ['FINANCE_MANAGER']],
  ['APPROVED', 'CANCELLED', ['BUYER']],
  ['IN_PRODUCTION', 'DISPUTED', ['PRODUCTION_MANAGER']],
  ['QUALITY_REVIEW', 'DISPUTED', ['QUALITY_INSPECTOR']],
  ['DELIVERED', 'DISPUTED', ['BUYER']],
];
function transition<S extends string>(
  current: S,
  next: S,
  roles: readonly CommerceRole[],
  edges: readonly Edge<S>[],
): S {
  const edge = edges.find(([from, to]) => from === current && to === next);
  requireRule(edge, 'INVALID_TRANSITION', 'This action is unavailable in the current state.');
  requireRule(
    edge[2].some((role) => roles.includes(role)),
    'FORBIDDEN',
    'Your current resource role cannot perform this action.',
  );
  return next;
}
export function transitionRfq(
  current: RfqState,
  next: RfqState,
  roles: readonly CommerceRole[],
  context: { quoteValid?: boolean; quoteExpired?: boolean } = {},
) {
  transition(current, next, roles, rfqEdges);
  if (next === 'ACCEPTED')
    requireRule(context.quoteValid, 'QUOTE_UNAVAILABLE', 'Accept the current unexpired quote.');
  if (next === 'EXPIRED')
    requireRule(context.quoteExpired, 'NOT_EXPIRED', 'The quote has not expired.');
  return next;
}
export function transitionOffer(
  current: OfferState,
  next: OfferState,
  roles: readonly CommerceRole[],
  context: { expiresAt: number; now: number },
) {
  transition(current, next, roles, offerEdges);
  requireRule(
    Number.isFinite(context.now) && Number.isFinite(context.expiresAt),
    'INVALID_DATE',
    'Valid offer timestamps are required.',
  );
  if (next === 'ACCEPTED')
    requireRule(context.now < context.expiresAt, 'OFFER_EXPIRED', 'This offer has expired.');
  if (next === 'EXPIRED')
    requireRule(context.now >= context.expiresAt, 'NOT_EXPIRED', 'This offer has not expired.');
  return next;
}
export function quantity(value: number, positive = false): number {
  requireRule(
    Number.isSafeInteger(value) && value >= (positive ? 1 : 0) && value <= 1000000,
    'INVALID_QUANTITY',
    'Use whole quantities between zero and one million.',
  );
  return value;
}
export type Fulfillment = {
  requested: number;
  reserved: number;
  allocated: number;
  produced: number;
  submitted: number;
  approved: number;
  rejected: number;
  pending: number;
  delivered: number;
};
export function reconcileFulfillment(q: Fulfillment): void {
  quantity(q.requested, true);
  for (const name of [
    'requested',
    'reserved',
    'allocated',
    'produced',
    'submitted',
    'approved',
    'rejected',
    'pending',
    'delivered',
  ] as const) {
    const value = q[name];
    quantity(value);
    requireRule(value <= q.requested, 'EXCESS_QUANTITY', `${name} exceeds requested quantity.`);
  }
  requireRule(
    q.allocated + q.reserved <= q.requested,
    'EXCESS_ALLOCATION',
    'Accepted and reserved quantities exceed this order.',
  );
  requireRule(
    q.produced <= q.allocated && q.submitted <= q.produced,
    'EXCESS_PRODUCTION',
    'Production cannot exceed accepted assignments.',
  );
  requireRule(
    q.approved + q.rejected + q.pending === q.submitted,
    'QA_MISMATCH',
    'Approved, rejected and pending quantities must equal submitted quantity.',
  );
  requireRule(
    q.delivered <= q.approved,
    'UNAPPROVED_DELIVERY',
    'Only QA-approved units may be delivered.',
  );
}
export function validateProgress(assigned: number, previous: number, cumulative: number) {
  quantity(assigned, true);
  quantity(previous);
  quantity(cumulative);
  requireRule(
    previous <= cumulative && cumulative <= assigned,
    'EXCESS_PRODUCTION',
    'Cumulative production must not decrease or exceed the accepted quantity.',
  );
}
export function reconcileInspection(
  submitted: number,
  approved: number,
  rejected: number,
  pending: number,
  previousApproved = 0,
) {
  for (const value of [submitted, approved, rejected, pending, previousApproved]) quantity(value);
  requireRule(
    approved + rejected + pending === submitted && approved >= previousApproved,
    'QA_MISMATCH',
    'QA totals must reconcile to submitted units and preserve previous approvals.',
  );
}
export function payableForUnits(unitMillimes: bigint, units: number): bigint {
  quantity(units);
  requireRule(
    unitMillimes >= 0n && unitMillimes <= MAX_TND_MILLIMES,
    'INVALID_AMOUNT',
    'Invalid TND unit amount.',
  );
  const total = unitMillimes * BigInt(units);
  requireRule(
    total <= MAX_TND_MILLIMES,
    'AMOUNT_OVERFLOW',
    'The total exceeds the supported TND limit.',
  );
  return total;
}
export function reconcileSettlement(
  eligible: bigint,
  settled: bigint,
  reserved: bigint,
  additional: bigint = 0n,
) {
  for (const value of [eligible, settled, reserved, additional])
    requireRule(
      value >= 0n && value <= MAX_TND_MILLIMES,
      'INVALID_AMOUNT',
      'Invalid settlement amount.',
    );
  requireRule(
    settled + reserved + additional <= eligible,
    'EXCESS_SETTLEMENT',
    'Payment exceeds the eligible outstanding amount.',
  );
}
export function transitionBatch(
  current: BatchState,
  next: BatchState,
  roles: readonly CommerceRole[],
  context: {
    assigned: number;
    produced: number;
    approved: number;
    pending: number;
    reworkAccepted?: boolean;
  },
) {
  transition(current, next, roles, batchEdges);
  validateProgress(context.assigned, 0, context.produced);
  quantity(context.approved);
  quantity(context.pending);
  requireRule(
    context.approved + context.pending <= context.produced,
    'QA_MISMATCH',
    'Quality counts cannot exceed produced units.',
  );
  if (next === 'SUBMITTED')
    requireRule(context.produced > 0, 'EMPTY_SUBMISSION', 'Produce units before submitting.');
  if (next === 'APPROVED' || next === 'COMPLETED')
    requireRule(
      context.approved === context.assigned && context.pending === 0,
      'QUALITY_REQUIRED',
      'All assigned units must be QA-approved.',
    );
  if (current === 'REWORK_REQUESTED' && next === 'IN_PROGRESS')
    requireRule(
      context.reworkAccepted,
      'CONSENT_REQUIRED',
      'The artisan must explicitly accept rework under the agreed terms.',
    );
  return next;
}
export function transitionPayment(
  current: PaymentState,
  next: PaymentState,
  roles: readonly CommerceRole[],
  context: { provenance: 'SYNTHETIC'; evidenceType?: 'SIMULATED_SETTLEMENT' },
) {
  transition(current, next, roles, paymentEdges);
  requireRule(
    context.provenance === 'SYNTHETIC',
    'LIVE_PAYMENT_FORBIDDEN',
    'Only isolated synthetic payments are supported.',
  );
  if (next === 'SETTLED')
    requireRule(
      context.evidenceType === 'SIMULATED_SETTLEMENT',
      'EVIDENCE_REQUIRED',
      'Synthetic settlement must be explicitly labelled as simulated.',
    );
  return next;
}
export type OrderContext = Fulfillment & {
  buyerDue: bigint;
  buyerSettled: bigint;
  artisanDue: bigint;
  artisanSettled: bigint;
  openDisputes: number;
  pendingPayments: number;
  materialsResolved: boolean;
};
export function transitionOrder(
  current: OrderState,
  next: OrderState,
  roles: readonly CommerceRole[],
  context: OrderContext,
) {
  transition(current, next, roles, orderEdges);
  quantity(context.openDisputes);
  quantity(context.pendingPayments);
  reconcileFulfillment(context);
  reconcileSettlement(context.buyerDue, context.buyerSettled, 0n);
  reconcileSettlement(context.artisanDue, context.artisanSettled, 0n);
  if (next === 'CANCELLED')
    requireRule(
      context.allocated === 0 &&
        context.reserved === 0 &&
        context.buyerSettled === 0n &&
        context.artisanDue === 0n &&
        context.pendingPayments === 0,
      'OBLIGATIONS_REMAIN',
      'Cancellation cannot erase accepted work or financial obligations.',
    );
  if (next === 'FUNDING_CONFIRMED')
    requireRule(
      context.buyerSettled === context.buyerDue,
      'FUNDING_REQUIRED',
      'Reconcile full simulated buyer funding first.',
    );
  if (next === 'IN_PRODUCTION')
    requireRule(
      context.allocated === context.requested && context.reserved === 0,
      'ALLOCATION_REQUIRED',
      'All requested units need explicit accepted assignments.',
    );
  if (next === 'QUALITY_REVIEW')
    requireRule(
      context.submitted === context.requested,
      'SUBMISSION_REQUIRED',
      'Submit all requested units before quality review.',
    );
  if (
    ['READY_TO_SHIP', 'IN_TRANSIT', 'DELIVERED', 'BUYER_ACCEPTED', 'SETTLED', 'CLOSED'].includes(
      next,
    )
  )
    requireRule(
      context.approved === context.requested && context.rejected === 0 && context.pending === 0,
      'QUALITY_REQUIRED',
      'Full QA approval is required.',
    );
  if (['BUYER_ACCEPTED', 'SETTLED', 'CLOSED'].includes(next))
    requireRule(
      context.delivered === context.requested,
      'DELIVERY_REQUIRED',
      'Reconcile delivered quantity first.',
    );
  if (next === 'SETTLED' || next === 'CLOSED')
    requireRule(
      context.buyerSettled === context.buyerDue &&
        context.artisanSettled === context.artisanDue &&
        context.openDisputes === 0 &&
        context.pendingPayments === 0,
      'OBLIGATIONS_REMAIN',
      'Outstanding balances and disputes block settlement/closure.',
    );
  if (next === 'CLOSED')
    requireRule(
      context.materialsResolved,
      'MATERIALS_UNRESOLVED',
      'Record the synthetic material disposition before closure.',
    );
  return next;
}


===== packages\contracts\src\commerce\metrics.ts =====

/** Versioned cumulative per-order metrics. Reporting window is order creation..asOf, UTC.
 * Integer quantities and decimal millime strings; ratios carry their denominator.
 * No actual cost/time or verified-bank sources exist: unavailable fields stay null. */
export const COMMERCE_METRICS_VERSION = 1;
export interface MetricSource {
  provenance: string;
  status: string;
  delivered: number;
  milestones?: { shipped: boolean; accepted: boolean };
  rfq: { quantity: number; provenance: string };
  batches: {
    provenance: string;
    produced: number;
    approved: number;
    submitted: number;
    offerId: string;
  }[];
  offers: { id: string; provenance: string; unitPayMillimes: bigint }[];
  payments: {
    provenance: string;
    kind: string;
    status: string;
    amountMillimes: bigint;
    evidenceType: string | null;
  }[];
}
export function deriveCommerceMetrics(source: MetricSource) {
  if (
    [source, source.rfq, ...source.batches, ...source.offers, ...source.payments].some(
      (r) => r.provenance !== 'SYNTHETIC',
    )
  )
    throw Error('Only synthetic commerce sources are supported.');
  const sum = (field: 'produced' | 'approved' | 'submitted') =>
    source.batches.reduce((n, b) => n + b[field], 0);
  const ratio = (numerator: number) => ({
    numerator,
    denominator: source.rfq.quantity,
    ratio: source.rfq.quantity === 0 ? null : numerator / source.rfq.quantity,
  });
  const approved = sum('approved');
  const shipped =
    source.milestones?.shipped ||
    ['IN_TRANSIT', 'DELIVERED', 'BUYER_ACCEPTED', 'SETTLED', 'CLOSED'].includes(source.status)
      ? approved
      : 0;
  const accepted =
    source.milestones?.accepted || ['BUYER_ACCEPTED', 'SETTLED', 'CLOSED'].includes(source.status)
      ? source.delivered
      : 0;
  const settled = (kind: string) =>
    source.payments
      .filter((p) => p.kind === kind && p.status === 'SETTLED')
      .reduce((n, p) => {
        if (p.evidenceType !== 'SIMULATED_SETTLEMENT')
          throw Error('Invalid settlement classification.');
        return n + p.amountMillimes;
      }, 0n);
  const earned = source.batches.reduce((n, b) => {
    const offer = source.offers.find((o) => o.id === b.offerId);
    if (!offer) throw Error('Missing authoritative offer.');
    return n + BigInt(b.approved) * offer.unitPayMillimes;
  }, 0n);
  const payout = settled('ARTISAN_PAYOUT');
  if (payout > earned) throw Error('Unreconciled payout.');
  return {
    definitionVersion: COMMERCE_METRICS_VERSION,
    provenance: 'SYNTHETIC',
    evidenceClass: 'SIMULATED',
    timezone: 'UTC',
    period: 'ORDER_LIFETIME_TO_AS_OF',
    fulfillment: {
      produced: ratio(sum('produced')),
      submitted: ratio(sum('submitted')),
      approved: ratio(approved),
      shipped: ratio(shipped),
      received: ratio(source.delivered),
      accepted: ratio(accepted),
    },
    finance: {
      currency: 'TND',
      unit: 'MILLIME',
      buyerReceived: settled('BUYER_RECEIPT').toString(),
      artisanEarned: earned.toString(),
      artisanPaid: payout.toString(),
      artisanOutstanding: (earned - payout).toString(),
      scheduledBuyerReceipt: source.payments
        .filter(
          (p) =>
            p.kind === 'BUYER_RECEIPT' && ['SCHEDULED', 'APPROVED', 'INITIATED'].includes(p.status),
        )
        .reduce((n, p) => n + p.amountMillimes, 0n)
        .toString(),
      scheduledArtisanPayout: source.payments
        .filter(
          (p) =>
            p.kind === 'ARTISAN_PAYOUT' &&
            ['SCHEDULED', 'APPROVED', 'INITIATED'].includes(p.status),
        )
        .reduce((n, p) => n + p.amountMillimes, 0n)
        .toString(),
      verifiedSettlement: null,
      actualCost: null,
      actualHours: null,
      coverage: {
        verifiedSettlement: 'UNAVAILABLE',
        actualCost: 'UNAVAILABLE',
        actualHours: 'UNAVAILABLE',
      },
    },
  };
}
export type CommerceMetrics = ReturnType<typeof deriveCommerceMetrics>;

===== packages\contracts\src\domain.ts =====

// Pure rules for implemented foundation workflows. No infrastructure dependencies.
export type ApprovalState = 'DRAFT' | 'PENDING_REVIEW' | 'APPROVED' | 'REJECTED' | 'SUSPENDED';
export function canEditOrganization(state: ApprovalState): boolean {
  return state === 'DRAFT' || state === 'REJECTED';
}
export function canReviewOrganization(
  state: ApprovalState,
  decision: 'APPROVED' | 'REJECTED' | 'SUSPENDED',
): boolean {
  return decision === 'SUSPENDED'
    ? state === 'APPROVED'
    : state === 'PENDING_REVIEW' || state === 'SUSPENDED';
}
export type Period = { effectiveFrom: Date; effectiveTo: Date };
export function isCapacityRevision(period: Period, overlaps: readonly Period[]): boolean {
  const start = period.effectiveFrom.getTime(),
    end = period.effectiveTo.getTime();
  return (
    Number.isFinite(start) &&
    Number.isFinite(end) &&
    start < end &&
    overlaps.every(
      (row) => row.effectiveFrom.getTime() === start && row.effectiveTo.getTime() === end,
    )
  );
}
// Decimal(12,2) persistence, application limit 100000; zero means no declared availability.
export function exactCapacityQuantity(quantity: number): string {
  if (
    !Number.isFinite(quantity) ||
    quantity < 0 ||
    quantity > 100000 ||
    !/^(0|[1-9]\d*)(\.\d{1,2})?$/.test(String(quantity))
  )
    throw new RangeError('Invalid capacity quantity.');
  return quantity.toFixed(2);
}
// Nonnegative TND only. Strings at API boundaries, bigint millimes internally.
export const MAX_TND_MILLIMES = 9223372036854775807n;
function bounded(value: bigint): bigint {
  if (value < 0n || value > MAX_TND_MILLIMES) throw new RangeError('TND amount is out of range.');
  return value;
}
export function parseTnd(value: string): bigint {
  if (typeof value !== 'string' || !/^(0|[1-9]\d{0,15})(\.\d{1,3})?$/.test(value))
    throw new RangeError('Use exact TND with at most three decimal places.');
  const [whole, fraction = ''] = value.split('.');
  return bounded(BigInt(whole) * 1000n + BigInt(fraction.padEnd(3, '0')));
}
export function formatTnd(millimes: bigint): string {
  bounded(millimes);
  return `${millimes / 1000n}.${String(millimes % 1000n).padStart(3, '0')}`;
}
export function addTnd(left: bigint, right: bigint): bigint {
  return bounded(bounded(left) + bounded(right));
}
// Explicit HALF_UP rounding, once, at the millime boundary (e.g. a rational rate).
export function prorateTnd(amount: bigint, numerator: bigint, denominator: bigint): bigint {
  bounded(amount);
  if (numerator < 0n || denominator <= 0n) throw new RangeError('Invalid nonnegative ratio.');
  const scaled = amount * numerator;
  return bounded(scaled / denominator + (2n * (scaled % denominator) >= denominator ? 1n : 0n));
}

import { z } from 'zod';

  name: z.string().trim().min(2).max(160),
  representativeName: z.string().trim().min(2).max(120),

  region: z.string().trim().min(1).max(120),

  PRODUCTION_MANAGER: ['organization.read', 'production.manage'],
  FINANCE_MANAGER: [

    'finance.payout.read',
    'finance.payout.approve',
  ],
  QUALITY_INSPECTOR: ['organization.read', 'quality.inspection.read', 'quality.inspection.create'],
  INVENTORY_LOGISTICS_COORDINATOR: ['organization.read', 'inventory.manage'],
  SUPPORT: ['organization.read', 'support.case.read', 'support.case.manage'],
  RESEARCHER_ANALYST: ['organization.read', 'analytics.aggregate.read'],
  PRODUCT_DESIGNER: ['organization.read', 'product.specification.manage'],
  BUSINESS_DEVELOPMENT: ['organization.read', 'buyer.relationship.manage'],
};
export function rolesForOrganization(type: string): BusinessRole[] {
  if (type === 'BUYER_BUSINESS') return ['BUYER_REPRESENTATIVE'];
  if (['ASSOCIATION', 'PARTNER_COOPERATIVE'].includes(type)) return ['ASSOCIATION_COORDINATOR'];
  if (type === 'INTERNAL') return ['NASJ_OPERATOR'];
  return [];
}
export function grantAllowed(type: string, permission: string) {
  return (
    (type === 'BUYER_BUSINESS' &&
      ['buyer.rfq.create', 'buyer.quotation.negotiate', 'buyer.quotation.approve'].includes(
        permission,
      )) ||
    (type === 'INTERNAL' &&
      ['operator.payout.initiate', 'operator.payout.approve'].includes(permission))
  );
}
export function permissionsForMembership(member: {
  isManager: boolean;
  roles: { role: BusinessRole }[];
  status: string;
  organization?: { approvalStatus: string; type?: string };
  permissionGrants?: { permission: string; enabled?: boolean }[];
}): Permission[] {
  if (member.status !== 'ACTIVE') return [];
  const permissions = new Set<Permission>(['organization.read']);
  for (const role of member.roles) {
    if (
      member.organization?.type &&
      !rolesForOrganization(member.organization.type).includes(role.role) &&
      !(member.organization.type === 'BUYER_BUSINESS' && role.role === 'BUYER') &&
      !(
        member.organization.type === 'INTERNAL' &&
        !['BUYER', 'BUYER_REPRESENTATIVE', 'ARTISAN', 'ASSOCIATION_COORDINATOR'].includes(role.role)
      )
    )
      continue;
    for (const permission of rolePermissions[role.role] ?? []) permissions.add(permission);
  }
  for (const grant of member.permissionGrants ?? [])
    if (
      grantAllowed(member.organization?.type ?? '', grant.permission) &&
      member.roles.some((r) =>
        member.organization?.type === 'BUYER_BUSINESS'
          ? ['BUYER', 'BUYER_REPRESENTATIVE'].includes(r.role)
          : r.role === 'NASJ_OPERATOR',
      )
    ) {
      if (grant.enabled === false) permissions.delete(grant.permission as Permission);
      else permissions.add(grant.permission as Permission);
    }
  if (member.isManager)
    for (const permission of orgManagement) {
      if (
        member.organization?.type &&
        member.organization.type !== 'BUYER_BUSINESS' &&
        permission !== 'organization.read' &&
        permission !== 'organization.update' &&
        permission !== 'organization.approval.request' &&
        permission !== 'organization.members.read' &&
        permission !== 'audit.read'
      )
        continue;
      permissions.add(permission);
    }
  if (member.organization && member.organization.approvalStatus !== 'APPROVED') {
    const governance: Permission[] = [
      'organization.read',
      'organization.update',
      'organization.approval.request',
      'organization.members.read',
    ];
    return [...permissions].filter((p) => governance.includes(p));
  }
  return [...permissions];
}

===== scripts\backup-database.ts =====

import { execFile } from 'node:child_process';
import { promisify } from 'node:util';
import { join } from 'node:path';
import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import {
  encryptBackup,
  packDatabaseBackup,
  readBackupConfiguration,
  pruneExpiredBackups,
  readBackupKey,
  writePrivateBackup,
} from '../apps/api/src/operations/backup.js';
// Container uses its existing PostgreSQL authentication. No password or connection URL in argv/logs.
const {
  BACKUP_CONTAINER: container,
  BACKUP_DIRECTORY: directory,
  BACKUP_KEY_FILE: keyFile,
  BACKUP_CONFIG_FILE: configFile,
  BACKUP_DATABASE_USER: user = 'foundation_test',
  BACKUP_DATABASE_NAME: database = 'foundation_test',
} = process.env;
try {
  if (
    !container ||
    !/^[a-zA-Z0-9][a-zA-Z0-9_.-]{0,127}$/.test(container) ||
    !directory ||
    !keyFile ||
    !/^[a-zA-Z0-9_]{1,63}$/.test(user) ||
    !/^[a-zA-Z0-9_]{1,63}$/.test(database)
  )
    throw Error('Invalid backup configuration.');
  const key = await readBackupKey(keyFile);
  const started = performance.now();
  const { stdout } = await promisify(execFile)(
    'docker',
    ['--context', 'default', 'exec', container, 'pg_dump', '-U', user, '-Fc', database],
    { encoding: 'buffer', maxBuffer: 64 * 1024 * 1024, timeout: 120000 },
  );
  const configuration = configFile ? await readBackupConfiguration(configFile) : undefined;
  const payload = packDatabaseBackup(stdout, configuration);
  const encrypted = encryptBackup(payload, key);
  payload.fill(0);
  configuration?.fill(0);
  key.fill(0);
  stdout.fill(0);
  const filename = `backup-${new Date().toISOString().replaceAll(':', '-')}-${randomUUID()}.hcab`;
  await writePrivateBackup(join(directory, filename), encrypted);
  const expiredRemoved = await pruneExpiredBackups(directory);
  console.log(
    JSON.stringify({
      code: 'BACKUP_CREATED',
      configurationIncluded: Boolean(configFile),
      expiredRemoved,
      filename,
      encryptedBytes: encrypted.length,
      durationMs: Math.round(performance.now() - started),
    }),
  );
} catch {
  console.error(JSON.stringify({ code: 'BACKUP_FAILED' }));
  process.exitCode = 1;
}

===== scripts\dev-demo-web.ts =====

import { readFile } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process';
import { parseEnv } from 'node:util';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';

const root = new URL('../', import.meta.url);
const values = parseEnv(await readFile(new URL('.local/demo.env', root), 'utf8'));
if (
  values.DEMO_MODE !== 'true' ||
  values.NODE_ENV !== 'development' ||
  values.PUBLIC_APP_URL !== 'http://127.0.0.1:3200' ||
  values.API_INTERNAL_URL !== 'http://127.0.0.1:3201' ||
  values.NEXT_DIST_DIR !== '.next-demo'
) {
  throw new Error('Run demo:setup to prepare the dedicated demo environment.');
}
// Load the environment before spawning Next. Passing --env-file to Next's Node
// process makes its worker forward that forbidden flag through NODE_OPTIONS.
const web = spawn(
  process.execPath,
  [
    fileURLToPath(new URL('apps/web/node_modules/next/dist/bin/next', root)),
    'dev',
    fileURLToPath(new URL('apps/web', root)),
    '--hostname',
    '127.0.0.1',
    '--port',
    '3200',
  ],
  { cwd: fileURLToPath(root), env: { ...process.env, ...values }, stdio: 'inherit' },
);
for (const signal of ['SIGINT', 'SIGTERM'] as const) {
  process.on(signal, () => web.kill(signal));
}
web.on('error', () => {
  console.error('Unable to start the demo web process.');
  process.exitCode = 1;
});
web.on('exit', (code) => {
  process.exitCode = code ?? 1;
});


===== scripts\dev.ts =====

import { spawn, type ChildProcess } from 'node:child_process';
import { mkdir, open, readFile, unlink } from 'node:fs/promises';
import { createServer } from 'node:net';
import { fileURLToPath } from 'node:url';
import { parseEnv } from 'node:util';
import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
import { assertLocalDevelopment } from './local-development.js';

const root = fileURLToPath(new URL('../', import.meta.url));
const local = new URL('../.local/', import.meta.url);
const lockPath = new URL('dev.lock', local);
const children = new Set<ChildProcess>();
const processGroups = new Set<number>();
let stopping = false;
let lockOwned = false;
let finish: (() => void) | undefined;
let environment = process.env;

async function lock() {
  await mkdir(local, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 });
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 2; attempt++) {
    try {
      const file = await open(lockPath, 'wx', 0o600);
      await file.writeFile(String(process.pid));
      await file.close();
      lockOwned = true;
      return;
    } catch (error) {
      if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code !== 'EEXIST') throw error;
      const pid = Number(await readFile(lockPath, 'utf8'));
      if (Number.isSafeInteger(pid) && pid > 0) {
        try {
          process.kill(pid, 0);
          throw new Error('NASJ is already starting or running. Use http://localhost:3000.');
        } catch (probe) {
          if ((probe as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code !== 'ESRCH') throw probe;
        }
      }
      if (!Number.isSafeInteger(pid) || pid <= 0)
        throw new Error('Another startup is initializing its lock. Retry shortly.');
      await unlink(lockPath);
    }
  }
  throw new Error('Unable to acquire the local startup lock.');
}
function signalChildren(signal: NodeJS.Signals) {
  if (process.platform === 'win32') {
    for (const child of children)
      if (child.exitCode === null && child.signalCode === null) child.kill(signal);
    return;
  }
  for (const pid of processGroups) {
    try {
      process.kill(-pid, signal);
    } catch (error) {
      if ((error as NodeJS.ErrnoException).code !== 'ESRCH') throw error;
    }
  }
}
async function shutdown() {
  if (stopping) return;
  stopping = true;
  signalChildren('SIGTERM');
  await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 1000));
  signalChildren('SIGKILL');
  finish?.();
}
function start(command: string, args: string[], cwd = root) {
  if (stopping) throw new Error('Startup cancelled.');
  const child = spawn(command, args, {
    cwd,
    env: environment,
    stdio: 'inherit',
    detached: process.platform !== 'win32',
    // Windows exposes pnpm as a .cmd shim, which Node only launches through a shell.
    // Arguments are fixed literals in this file, never user input.
    shell: process.platform === 'win32' && command === 'pnpm',
  });
  children.add(child);
  if (child.pid) processGroups.add(child.pid);
  child.once('exit', () => children.delete(child));
  return child;
}
async function run(command: string, args: string[], cwd = root) {
  const child = start(command, args, cwd);
  await new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
    child.once('error', () => reject(new Error(`Unable to start ${command}.`)));
    child.once('exit', (code) =>
      code === 0
        ? resolve()
        : reject(new Error(`${command} preparation step failed. Review the output above.`)),
    );
  });
  if (child.pid) processGroups.delete(child.pid);
}
async function localServices() {
  type Probe = {
    connect(): Promise<void>;
    query(sql: string): Promise<unknown>;
    end(): Promise<void>;
  };
  const { Client } = createRequire(new URL('../apps/api/package.json', import.meta.url))('pg') as {
    Client: new (options: {
      connectionString: string | undefined;
      connectionTimeoutMillis: number;
    }) => Probe;
  };
  const database = new Client({
    connectionString: environment.DATABASE_URL,
    connectionTimeoutMillis: 1500,
  });
  let postgres = false;
  try {
    await database.connect();
    await database.query('SELECT 1');
    postgres = true;
  } catch {
  } finally {
    await database.end().catch(() => {});
  }
  let mailpit = false;
  try {
    const response = await fetch('http://127.0.0.1:8026/api/v1/info', {
      signal: AbortSignal.timeout(1500),
    });
    const info = (await response.json()) as { Version?: unknown };
    mailpit = response.ok && typeof info.Version === 'string';
  } catch {}
  return { postgres, mailpit };
}
async function checkPort(port: number) {
  const probe = createServer();
  try {
    await new Promise<void>((resolve, reject) => {
      probe.once('error', reject);
      probe.listen(port, () => probe.close(() => resolve()));
    });
  } catch {
    throw new Error(
      `Port ${port} is already occupied. Stop the previous project server, then run pnpm dev again; the launcher will not terminate an unrelated process.`,
    );
  }
}
async function ready(url: string, child: ChildProcess) {
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 120; attempt++) {
    if (stopping || child.exitCode !== null || child.signalCode !== null)
      throw new Error('Application exited during startup.');
    try {
      const response = await fetch(url, { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(1000), redirect: 'manual' });
      if (response.ok) return;
    } catch {}
    await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 250));
  }
  throw new Error('Application readiness timed out. Review the service output above.');
}
for (const signal of ['SIGINT', 'SIGTERM'] as const) {
  process.once(signal, () => {
    void shutdown();
  });
}
try {
  if (process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production')
    throw new Error(
      'pnpm dev is a local development entrypoint. Use the production deployment procedure.',
    );
  await lock();
  await checkPort(3000);
  await checkPort(3001);
  await run('pnpm', ['setup:local']);
  const values = parseEnv(await readFile(new URL('../.env', import.meta.url), 'utf8'));
  assertLocalDevelopment(values);
  // Preparation, API, browser rewrite and server rendering use the same explicit environment.
  environment = {
    ...process.env,
    ...values,
    MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL: values.DATABASE_URL,
    NEXT_DIST_DIR: '.next',
    NODE_ENV: 'development',
    DEMO_MODE: 'false',
    API_HOST: '127.0.0.1',
    API_PORT: '3001',
    API_INTERNAL_URL: 'http://127.0.0.1:3001',
    SMTP_HOST: '127.0.0.1',
    SMTP_PORT: '1026',
  };
  console.log('Preparing NASJ local services and accounts…');
  const services = await localServices();
  const missing = [!services.postgres ? 'postgres' : '', !services.mailpit ? 'mailpit' : ''].filter(
    Boolean,
  );
  if (missing.length)
    await run('docker', [
      '--context',
      'default',
      'compose',
      '-p',
      'nasj',
      'up',
      '-d',
      '--wait',
      ...missing,
    ]);
  else console.log('Reusing the healthy PostgreSQL and Mailpit services configured in .env.');
  await run('pnpm', ['--filter', '@nasj/contracts', 'build']);
  await run('pnpm', ['db:generate']);
  await run('pnpm', ['db:migrate']);
  await run('pnpm', [
    'exec',
    'tsx',
    '--tsconfig',
    'apps/api/tsconfig.json',
    'scripts/seed-local.ts',
  ]);
  const api = start(process.execPath, [
    fileURLToPath(new URL('../node_modules/tsx/dist/cli.mjs', import.meta.url)),
    'watch',
    '--tsconfig',
    'apps/api/tsconfig.json',
    'apps/api/src/main.ts',
  ]);
  const watchFailure = (child: ChildProcess) => {
    child.once('error', () => {
      if (!stopping) {
        process.exitCode = 1;
        void shutdown();
      }
    });
    child.once('exit', () => {
      if (!stopping) {
        process.exitCode = 1;
        void shutdown();
      }
    });
  };
  watchFailure(api);
  await ready('http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/health/ready', api);
  const web = start(process.execPath, [
    fileURLToPath(new URL('../apps/web/node_modules/next/dist/bin/next', import.meta.url)),
    'dev',
    'apps/web',
    '--hostname',
    'localhost',
    '--port',
    '3000',
  ]);
  watchFailure(web);
  await ready('http://localhost:3000', web);
  console.log(
    '\nNASJ ready: http://localhost:3000\nAccounts: .local/dev-credentials.json\nMail inbox: http://localhost:8026\nPress Ctrl+C to stop the API and web. Database records are preserved.\n',
  );
  await new Promise<void>((resolve) => {
    finish = resolve;
    if (stopping) resolve();
  });
} catch (error) {
  if (!stopping) {
    console.error(error instanceof Error ? error.message : 'Unable to start local development.');
    process.exitCode = 1;
  }
  await shutdown();
} finally {
  if (lockOwned) await unlink(lockPath).catch(() => {});
}


===== scripts\local-development.ts =====

/** The one-command launcher is deliberately limited to this project's local services. */
export function assertLocalDevelopment(values: Record<string, string | undefined>) {
  let database: URL;
  try {
    database = new URL(values.DATABASE_URL ?? '');
  } catch {
    throw new Error('The local DATABASE_URL is invalid. Run pnpm setup:local.');
  }
  if (
    values.NODE_ENV !== 'development' ||
    values.DEMO_MODE === 'true' ||
    !['postgres:', 'postgresql:'].includes(database.protocol) ||
    database.hostname !== '127.0.0.1' ||
    database.port !== '5442' ||
    database.pathname !== '/nasj' ||
    database.username !== 'nasj' ||
    database.search ||
    database.hash ||
    values.PUBLIC_APP_URL !== 'http://localhost:3000' ||
    (values.API_HOST ?? '127.0.0.1') !== '127.0.0.1' ||
    (values.API_PORT ?? '3001') !== '3001' ||
    (values.API_INTERNAL_URL ?? 'http://127.0.0.1:3001') !== 'http://127.0.0.1:3001' ||
    (values.SMTP_HOST ?? '127.0.0.1') !== '127.0.0.1' ||
    values.SMTP_PORT !== '1026'
  ) {
    throw new Error(
      'pnpm dev requires the local development configuration: localhost:3000, API 3001, PostgreSQL nasj at 127.0.0.1:5442 and local SMTP 1026. Production and remote databases cannot be seeded by this launcher.',
    );
  }
}


===== scripts\recover-organization-manager.ts =====

import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto';
import { emailSchema, resourceIdSchema } from '../packages/contracts/src/index.js';
import { loadConfig } from '../apps/api/src/config/env.js';
import { PrismaService } from '../apps/api/src/database/prisma.service.js';

const args = process.argv.slice(2).filter((value) => value !== '--');
const allowed = new Set(['--organization', '--email', '--operator', '--reason']);
const flags = new Map<string, string>();
let valid = args.length === 8;
for (let i = 0; i < args.length; i += 2) {
  const flag = args[i];
  const value = args[i + 1];
  if (!allowed.has(flag) || flags.has(flag) || !value || value.startsWith('--')) valid = false;
  else flags.set(flag, value.trim());
}
const organization = resourceIdSchema.safeParse(flags.get('--organization'));
const email = emailSchema.safeParse(flags.get('--email'));
const operator = emailSchema.safeParse(flags.get('--operator'));
const reason = flags.get('--reason') ?? '';
if (
  !valid ||
  !organization.success ||
  !email.success ||
  !operator.success ||
  reason.length < 5 ||
  reason.length > 500
) {
  console.error(
    'Usage: pnpm db:recover-organization-manager -- --organization <id> --email <active-verified-account> --operator <active-verified-admin> --reason <5-500 characters>',
  );
  process.exit(1);
}
const db = new PrismaService(loadConfig());
try {
  const result = await db.$transaction(
    async (tx) => {
      await tx.$executeRaw`SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(724631902)`;
      await tx.$executeRaw`SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(724631903)`;
      const [target, actingOperator, org] = await Promise.all([
        tx.user.findUnique({
          where: { email: email.data },
          select: { id: true, emailVerified: true, status: true },
        }),
        tx.user.findUnique({
          where: { email: operator.data },
          select: { id: true, emailVerified: true, status: true, role: true },
        }),
        tx.organization.findUnique({
          where: { id: organization.data },
          select: { id: true, type: true },
        }),
      ]);
      if (
        !org ||
        !target?.emailVerified ||
        target.status !== 'ACTIVE' ||
        !actingOperator?.emailVerified ||
        actingOperator.status !== 'ACTIVE' ||
        actingOperator.role !== 'ADMIN'
      ) {
        throw new Error('Recovery prerequisites were not met.');
      }
      const existing = await tx.organizationMember.findUnique({
        where: {
          organizationId_userId: { organizationId: org.id, userId: target.id },
        },
      });
      const defaultRoles =
        org.type === 'BUYER_BUSINESS'
          ? ['BUYER' as const]
          : org.type === 'ASSOCIATION'
            ? ['ASSOCIATION_COORDINATOR' as const]
            : [];
      const membership = await tx.organizationMember.upsert({
        where: {
          organizationId_userId: { organizationId: org.id, userId: target.id },
        },
        create: {
          organizationId: org.id,
          userId: target.id,
          isManager: true,
          status: 'ACTIVE',
          roles: {
            create: defaultRoles.map((role) => ({ role, assignedByUserId: actingOperator.id })),
          },
        },
        update: { isManager: true, status: 'ACTIVE', suspendedAt: null, revokedAt: null },
      });
      await tx.auditEvent.create({
        data: {
          actorId: actingOperator.id,
          targetType: 'OrganizationMember',
          targetId: membership.id,
          organizationId: org.id,
          action: 'organization.manager.recover',
          reason,
          correlationId: randomUUID(),
          before: {
            existed: Boolean(existing),
            status: existing?.status ?? null,
            isManager: existing?.isManager ?? false,
          },
          after: {
            userId: target.id,
            status: 'ACTIVE',
            isManager: true,
            source: 'TRUSTED_OPERATOR_CLI',
          },
        },
      });
      return { organizationId: org.id, userId: target.id };
    },
    { maxWait: 15000, timeout: 15000 },
  );
  console.log(
    `Organization manager recovered: organization=${result.organizationId} account=${result.userId}`,
  );
} catch {
  console.error(
    'Recovery failed. Verify database readiness, organization, active verified target account and active verified administrator operator.',
  );
  process.exitCode = 1;
} finally {
  await db.$disconnect();
}


===== scripts\role-migration-preflight.ts =====

import { createRequire } from 'node:module';
import { writeFile, mkdir } from 'node:fs/promises';
const { Client } = createRequire(new URL('../apps/api/package.json', import.meta.url))('pg') as {
  Client: new (options: {
    connectionString: string | undefined;
  }) => {
    connect(): Promise<void>;
    end(): Promise<void>;
    query(sql: string): Promise<{ rows: Record<string, unknown>[]; rowCount: number | null }>;
  };
};
const client = new Client({ connectionString: process.env.DATABASE_URL });
try {
  await client.connect();
  const coordinators = await client.query(
    `SELECT m."userId",array_agg(m."organizationId") AS "organizationIds" FROM "OrganizationMember" m JOIN "MembershipRole" r ON r."membershipId"=m.id WHERE m.status='ACTIVE' AND r.role='ASSOCIATION_COORDINATOR' GROUP BY m."userId" HAVING count(*)>1`,
  );
  const artisans = await client.query(
    `SELECT "artisanProfileId",array_agg("organizationId") AS "organizationIds" FROM "AssociationMembership" WHERE status='ACTIVE' AND "endedAt" IS NULL GROUP BY "artisanProfileId" HAVING count(*)>1`,
  );
  const legacy = await client.query(
    `SELECT r.role,count(*)::int AS count FROM "MembershipRole" r WHERE r.role::text NOT IN ('BUYER_REPRESENTATIVE','NASJ_OPERATOR','ASSOCIATION_COORDINATOR') GROUP BY r.role`,
  );
  const counts = await client.query(
    `SELECT (SELECT count(*)::int FROM "User") AS users,(SELECT count(*)::int FROM "Account") AS accounts,(SELECT count(*)::int FROM "Session") AS sessions,(SELECT count(*)::int FROM "ArtisanProfile") AS artisans`,
  );
  const report = {
    coordinatorConflicts: coordinators.rows,
    artisanConflicts: artisans.rows,
    legacyRolesForReview: legacy.rows,
    counts: counts.rows[0],
    safeToMigrate: coordinators.rowCount === 0 && artisans.rowCount === 0,
  };
  await mkdir('.local', { recursive: true });
  await writeFile('.local/role-migration-preflight.json', JSON.stringify(report, null, 2), {
    mode: 0o600,
  });
  console.log(
    JSON.stringify({
      safeToMigrate: report.safeToMigrate,
      coordinatorConflictCount: coordinators.rowCount,
      artisanConflictCount: artisans.rowCount,
      counts: report.counts,
    }),
  );
  if (!report.safeToMigrate) process.exitCode = 1;
} finally {
  await client.end();
}
